topic: Weapons, gadgets, classes, damage and ballistics

text:
WARDOGS has no fixed class selection at spawn. Each life, a player spends cash at a vendor to build a custom loadout of weapons, gear, utility and vehicles, starting from $10,000 [1]. Experience is earned on six role tracks, named in the official Season 1 changelog as Career, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver and Pilot, which gate which items can be bought [2]. "Assault" is a guide name, not an official one [10].

The developer's stance on realism is a middle line: the store page says "tactical gunplay" [1], the February 2026 FAQ calls the game "a hardcore shooter that doesn't forget it's a game" with "Grounded Gunplay" as an Early Access feature [6], and a May 2026 post lists "real-world ballistics" among its pillars [7]. No official weapon list, damage value or ballistic parameter has been published. This revision replaces press summaries with the full official Steam text for the 9 Sep Season 1 changelog [2], the 30 Sep update 0.1.2 [3] and the 2 Oct balance hotfix [4].

Document confidence is Medium: the structural model, role tracks, repricing and balance changes are official, but weapon-level names, prices and stats remain beta-era press or player-reported guides (see weapons-catalogue).

text:
- Loadouts are bought with cash each life from a vendor; players start with $10,000 and cash persists between matches (Steam page, checked 2026-10-08) [1].
- There is no spawn-time class pick. Six role tracks (Career, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver, Pilot) are named in the official changelog of 9 Sep 2026 [2]; an account-wide WARDOG Level is player-reported only [10].
- Official gunplay wording: "tactical gunplay" on the store page [1]; "a hardcore shooter that doesn't forget it's a game" and "Grounded Gunplay" (18 Feb 2026) [6]; "real-world ballistics" (21 May 2026) [7].
- Season 1 changelog (posted 9 Sep 2026, live for the 10 Sep launch) slowed role XP between levels 10 and 20, moved many unlocks and repriced hammers, scopes, the FOB and vehicles; the developer says each season gets a different XP curve and item order [2].
- Patch 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026) made revive validity server authoritative, scaled buildable-destruction rewards by build progress, barred throwables from enclosed vehicle seats and fixed a Havoc bug that raised damage taken from 20mm and 30mm cannon fire [3].
- Balance hotfix (2 Oct 2026): IR Rangefinders were disabled in the vendor until Season 02, when they will need batteries, and the CIWS now destroys a Havoc in about 6 s instead of 12 s [4].
- No official damage, headshot, armor or bullet-drop figures exist; the beta-era claim that drop and travel time are modelled is press-reported only [9].

Covers infantry combat, weapon categories, gadgets and equipment, the role/progression system as it relates to loadouts, the documented damage/ballistics model, and how loadout purchasing ties to the in-match economy. Game version: Early Access Season 1 through patch 0.1.2 and the 2 Oct 2026 hotfixes.

Excluded: vehicle combat detail (see vehicles-outposts-foundation), mode rules (gameplay-modes-foundation), full economy mechanics (economy-foundation) and per-weapon, per-item and per-price tables, which live in the depth documents listed under Related Documents.

text:
- **Loadout**: the set of weapons, gear, utility and vehicles bought for one life [1].
- **Role track**: a per-role XP progression that gates item purchases. The official track names are Career, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver and Pilot [2].
- **WARDOG Level**: account-wide level that unlocks general items such as armor, backpacks, ammo types and sidearms (player-reported; not defined in any official post read) [10].
- **Re-buy Loadout**: vendor option that rebuilds the previous kit after death (player-reported; no official post mentions it) [10].

- Update 0.1.2 is dated 30 Sep 2026 [3]. On 2 Oct 2026 two separate official posts appeared: a hotfix notice for 08:00 UTC about "minor security and stability issues" [5] and the balance hotfix on IR Rangefinders and the CIWS [4].
- Season 02 is announced for 15 Oct 2026; the 0.1.2 post says it will bring "new map conditions, equipment, balance reworks and additional features" [3][8].

text:
## Loadout selection and economy

Loadouts are purchased at a vendor each life [1]. The official posts do not describe the death cost or any re-buy feature; those details are player-reported (see death-penalty-and-rebuy) [10]. A guide dated 17 Sep 2026 reports that a level requirement only unlocks the option to buy, after which a one-time unlock payment is needed and the item then has a normal per-life vendor price [10] (player-reported). The official changelog does list vendor prices separately from track prices, which is consistent with that two-price model: for example Large Hammer has a vendor price ($1,600 to $2,400) and a Support track price ($25,000 to $75,000) [2].

Official equipment-space change: 155mm, 122mm and flare deployables take up more loadout space since the Season 1 changelog [2]. Per-item unlock costs from guides (medical gear, sidearms, parachute) are in gadgets-armor-and-equipment and weapons-catalogue rather than repeated here.

## Weapon categories and notable weapons

Official text names very few weapons: the Deagle (Career 90 to 85), the PP-19 50-round drum magazine (Medic 33 to 29), 762x54mm AP and 556mm AP ammo, and Recon 6-10x MRAD and MOA scopes [2]. Rocket launchers appear on the store page [1]. Everything else is beta-era press or player-reported [9][10].

A beta press table grouped the vendor into assault rifles, SMGs, shotguns, LMGs, marksman rifles, sniper rifles, a compound bow, sidearms and launchers (RPG-7, MAAWS, 9K333 Verba surface-to-air), recorded 33 weapons with 37 expected at launch, and said prices were not confirmed as final [9]. Those values predate the Season 1 repricing [2] and are stale; the full roster with prices and levels is in weapons-catalogue (confidence Low there).

## Roles and progression

Official: the Season 1 changelog names six tracks, Career, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver and Pilot, and lists unlock moves under Career, Medic, Support and Driver [2]. The beta press mapping of kills to four tracks (assault rifles and sidearms, SMGs, shotguns/LMGs/launchers, marksman/sniper/bow) used the guide name "Assault" and predates launch [9]; whether Career is a rename of that track is not stated officially (see progression-and-role-tracks). Guides add that Driver and Pilot are levelled by vehicles [10] (player-reported).

Season 1 changes (changelog posted 9 Sep 2026) [2]:

- Role-track XP requirements rose sharply in the middle band: level 6 from 8,750 to 9,250, level 10 from 25,000 to 35,000, level 15 from 54,750 to 110,000, level 20 from 111,500 to 250,000, level 25 from 192,000 to 325,000; levels below 6 unchanged, and the curve flattens from level 35 onward (level 50 is 1,000,000). The developer says median players at 20 to 25 hours will be around level 20.
- Career unlock moves: Deagle 90 to 85, Artillery Tank 55 to 90, Sports Parachute 36 to 35, Large Backpack 56 to 55, 762x54mm AP 83 to 82, 556mm AP 85 to 83. Medic: PP-19 50-round drum 33 to 29. Support: Large Hammer 7 to 8. Driver: Heavy Tank now Driver 35, plus nine other vehicle level moves.
- Recon scopes repriced: 6-10x MRAD $25,000 to $40,000; 6-10x MOA $30,000 to $45,000.
- Support track prices: Medium Hammer unlock $10,000 to $25,000; Large Hammer unlock $25,000 to $75,000. Vendor prices: Large Hammer $1,600 to $2,400; Forward Operating Base $2,500 to $7,500.
- Air vehicle player-kill XP lowered from 300 to 250.

Full ladders and price lists are in progression-unlock-tables and price-tables-season-1.

## Damage and ballistics

No official damage values, armor ratings or ballistic tables exist. The official statements are positional: "tactical gunplay" [1], "a hardcore shooter that doesn't forget it's a game" and "Grounded Gunplay" [6], and "real-world ballistics, audio and flight models" in a May 2026 post whose substance is in a video not captured as text [7]. Press from the closed beta reports that real bullet drop and travel time are modelled and that weapon weights differ (for example AMR 50 12.5 kg, LMGs 7.5 kg) [9]; this is not confirmed by the developer.

Official combat-relevant fixes: update 0.1.2 fixed a Havoc bug causing increased damage from 20mm and 30mm cannon fire and fixed buildable "crit spots" reappearing in the same place or jumping to the far side of a structure, so they now favour a spot reachable from where the player stands [3]. The 2 Oct hotfix halved the CIWS kill time on a Havoc (about 12 s to about 6 s), which the developer calls correcting an overcorrection in the previous patch [4]. See damage-ballistics-and-balance for the full record.

## Gadgets and utility

Officially named: ghillie suit, rocket launchers and forward operating bases [1]; grenades, smoke and C4 as throwables, parachutes, backpacks, flares, hammers and IR Rangefinders [2][3][4]. Player-reported: first aid kit, defibrillator, adrenaline pen and an Emergency Resuscitator [10]; see gadgets-armor-and-equipment. The 2 Oct post title says "IR Goggles" while its body says "IR Rangefinders"; whether these are one item is not stated [4].

title: Damage, Ballistics & Balance Changes
topic: Damage model, ballistics, hit registration, and the balance-change history

text:
The developer has never published a damage table, ballistic table, hit-registration description or armor rating for WARDOGS. What exists officially is a philosophy: the game is "a hardcore shooter that doesn't forget it's a game", with "real-world ballistics, audio and flight models" claimed in a May 2026 devlog summary [2][3][4]. No official text says what that means in numbers, and no official text mentions bullet drop or bullet travel time.

The official balance record is a short list of patch posts. The only post with a large, itemised balance section is the Season 1 changelog of 9 to 10 Sep 2026, and it is almost entirely progression and economy tuning (XP bands, unlock levels, prices), not weapon damage [6]. Combat-damage changes are rare: one Havoc cannon-damage bug fix in update 0.1.2 [8], and a 2 Oct 2026 hotfix that shortened the time the CIWS takes to destroy a Havoc from about 12 s to about 6 s and disabled IR Rangefinders in the vendor [9].

Document confidence is Medium. Every balance entry rests on official Steam posts (High), but the realism, ballistics and hit-registration sections rest on a few sentences of marketing-register text plus one beta-era press report, and the main conclusion is that the topic is largely undocumented.

- Official stance: "WARDOGS is a hardcore shooter that doesn't forget it's a game", aiming to balance "gameplay depth and accessibility" (Feb 2026, Jun 2026) [3][4].
- Official claim, pre-launch: "Real-world ballistics, audio and flight models" (21 May 2026 post summary) [2]. The video behind it was not available as text, so the specifics are unknown.
- The Steam store page (snapshot 2026-10-08) says "tactical gunplay" and does not contain the phrase "realistic gunplay tuned for gameplay" that the foundation document attributes to it; see Open Questions [1].

- Combat-relevant balance changes in the official record: Havoc 20mm/30mm damage-taken bug fix (30 Sep 2026) [8]; CIWS-versus-Havoc kill time roughly 12 s to roughly 6 s and IR Rangefinders removed from the vendor until Season 02 (2 Oct 2026) [9].
- Season 1 changelog (10 Sep 2026) balance is progression-centred: 10 XP-band changes, 6 Career, 1 Medic, 1 Support and 10 Driver unlock-level moves, and 14 vendor price changes [6].
- The developer says each season will have "a different XP curve with different item orders", so these baseline values are expected to change at Season 02 [6][8][11].

## What the developer has said about realism versus tuning

| 2026-02-18 | "WARDOGS - Top Questions" [4] | "MILSIM? ARCADE? WARDOGS is a hardcore shooter that doesn't forget it's a game. Aiming to balance gameplay depth and accessibility. Every decision matters. From moment-to-moment gunfights to Progression Unlocks." Setting described as "grounded militaristic gameplay"; Early Access feature list includes "Grounded Gunplay & Vehicles". Custom "WAR DYNAMICS FRAMEWORK" on UE5; the post says the team is "heavily conscious of performance & input latency" | Official |
| 2026-03-03 | "Answering Your Questions" [5] | Video Q&A (100 players and 3 teams, monetisation, console release). The saved text has no combat content, so nothing on damage or ballistics can be cited from it | Official |
| 2026-05-21 | "Tactical Depth & Teamplay" [2] | "Real-world ballistics, audio and flight models"; "every bullet fired, every loadout built, and every second-to-second choice has real consequences for your account balance" | Official (marketing register) |
| 2026-06-06 | "Gameplay Trailer" [12] | "Play it slow, tactical and methodical, OR embrace the hardcore shooter that doesn't forget it's a game"; the game was shown in pre-alpha | Official |
| 2026-06-16 | "Addressing Feedback" [3] | "Every player's line between arcade and realistic is different. We've drawn ours. This isn't just about Killcam." Approach applies "throughout Early Access & Beyond" | Official |

Assessment: the developer's stated position is a deliberate middle between milsim and arcade, with the line left to the developer (High confidence that this is the stated position; evidence [3][4]). Where the line sits for any specific mechanic (damage falloff, recoil, time-to-kill) is not stated in text (Low confidence on any such inference; no evidence either way).

The 16 Jun 2026 post names "Killcam" explicitly, which implies a killcam feature was a feedback topic. The post text does not say whether a killcam exists in the Early Access build or how it was changed [3]. This is recorded in Open Questions.

## Bullet drop and bullet travel as documented

- Official sources: none. No saved Steam post and not the store page mention bullet drop, bullet velocity, travel time, gravity, zeroing or range tables [1][2][3][4][6][7][8][9]. The only official hook is the phrase "Real-world ballistics" [2].
- Press (beta era): the foundation document cites an allthings.how beta write-up reporting that real bullet drop and travel time are modelled and that carried weights differ (for example AMR 50 12.5 kg, LMGs 7.5 kg) [13]. This is press, drawn from closed-beta play, and is not confirmed by the developer. It is consistent with, but does not prove, the "real-world ballistics" claim [2].
- Related fix: the Season 1 changelog lists "Fixed a DPI issue affecting tank aiming"; that concerns input scaling on vehicle weapons, not ballistic behaviour [6].
- Related change: "Vehicle turrets now have a maximum operator rotation speed" (Season 1 changelog) [6].

## Damage model and hit registration as documented

| Topic | What is officially documented | Source |
|-------|-------------------------------|--------|
| Weapon damage values, headshot multipliers, falloff | Nothing | [1][2][3][4][6][8][9] |
| Armor ratings, plate or vest damage reduction | Nothing. The Season 1 changelog mentions only a Sports Parachute, Large Backpack and ammo-type unlocks, not armor stats | [6] |
| Ammo types | "762x54mm AP" and "556mm AP" exist as Career unlocks; their damage effect is not described | [6] |
| Hit registration or netcode for hit validation | Revive validity checks are "fully server authoritative" (0.1.2). Hit validation itself is not described. The team states performance and input latency are priorities | [4][8] |
| Buildable damage | "Crit spots" on buildables were fixed to stop reappearing in the same place or jumping to the far side of a structure; they "now favour a spot you can reach from where you're standing". Destruction rewards "scale with their build progress" | [8] |
| Vehicle and air damage | Havoc bug "causing increased damage taken from 20mm and 30mm cannon fire" fixed (0.1.2); CIWS kill time on a Havoc about 12 s down to about 6 s (hotfix) | [8][9] |
| Killcam | Named in a devlog title context only | [3] |

## Chronological list of balance changes in each official patch post

Source posts: Season 1 changelog posted 2026-09-09 22:46 UTC (published as the launch-day pre-load) [6]; Launch Stability Hotfix #1 of 2026-09-10 [10]; Patch 0.11 post of 2026-09-12 (deployed 14 Sep) [7]; Update 0.1.2 of 2026-09-30 [8]; Security & Stability Hotfix notice of 2026-10-02 [14]; IR Goggles & CIWS Balance Hotfix of 2026-10-02 [9].

### 1. Season 1 changelog (9 to 10 Sep 2026) [6]

Developer-filed "Gameplay and vehicles":

- Z20 Lakota balance pass, plus a fix for sluggish pitch.
- Helicopter input damping now applies to every input device.
- Vehicle turrets now have a maximum operator rotation speed.
- 155mm, 122mm and flare deployables now take up more room in the loadout.
- Fixed a DPI issue affecting tank aiming.
- Z20 Lakota chase-camera rotation rattle reduced by 6 dB.

Developer-filed "Balance changes" (italic rationale in the post): levels roughly 10 to 20 slowed, the curve flattened from 35 onward, "our median players, at 20 to 25 hours, will be around level 20", and "the top 5%" who want the "big ticket items" will have to grind. Artillery moves to Career 90 and Heavy Tank to Driver 35; Driver "rejigged to give a satisfying escalation through attack vehicles"; Forward Operating Base and Large Hammer vendor prices raised "to make them more of a choice".

"XP Bands": "Previously our balancing was designed specifically for weekend long beta tests. Now they will be in-line with where we believe they should be. Each season we will have a different XP curve with different item orders." Values are in the Baseline table below.

"XP Events": player kill using an air vehicle 300 to 250 XP; supply crate item sold under $75 25 XP to 1 XP.

"Economy Changes": 14 vendor and role-track price changes and a rescaled supply-crate purchase curve (Baseline table). "Season 1.0 Unlocks" lists Career, Medic, Support and Driver level moves (Baseline table). No weapon damage, recoil or range change appears in this post.

### 2. Launch Stability Hotfix #1 (10 Sep 2026) [10]

Client hotfix for server joins, kicks and login queue. No balance or damage content.

### 3. Patch 0.11 (announced 12 Sep, deployed 14 Sep 2026) [7]

Server browser, community-server discoverability, Asian capacity, and an economy-abuse policy. No weapon, damage or unlock changes. The only balance-adjacent items are "Various cash exploits have been fixed", a temporary "5% End of Match cash bonus" on community servers "for the next week", and the abuse sanctions (timed ban plus cash and XP reset for exploits; permanent ban for exploit tutorials and XP-farming servers). The post says Season 2 content is not affected by the quality-of-life queue.

### 4. Update 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026, maintenance at 08:00 UTC) [8]

Balance- or combat-relevant items only:

- Revive action validity checks now fully server authoritative.
- Vehicle fly-through exploit fixed; rewards capped.
- Buildable-destruction rewards now scale with build progress, so destroying a placed schematic no longer gives a full reward.
- Depositing pallets into a FOB outside the zone awards reduced rewards.
- Throwables (grenades, smoke, C4) can no longer be used from enclosed vehicle seats.
- Adaptive crosshair now hides while aiming down sights.
- Buildable crit spots no longer reappear in the same place, get pushed into corners, or jump to the far side; they favour a spot reachable from the player's position.
- Havoc bug fixed that "caus[ed] increased damage taken from 20mm and 30mm cannon fire".

The post states that Season 02 will include "balance reworks" [8]. No numeric weapon values are given.

### 5. Security & Stability Hotfix notice (2 Oct 2026) [14]

Scheduled 08:00 UTC, about one hour downtime, for minor security and stability issues. No balance content.

### 6. IR Goggles & CIWS Balance Hotfix (2 Oct 2026, 15:39 UTC) [9]

- IR Rangefinders will be disabled in the vendor, once servers restart across regions within 12 hours, "until Season 02, where they will require batteries to use". Reason given: "we agree with player sentiment and they cross the line into being too overpowered."
- The CIWS "now destroys the havoc in around 6 seconds as opposed to 12". "We acknowledge we overcorrected this in the previous patch."
- "No new client download or server downtime is required."

text:
This document is a pre-Season-02 baseline of the non-weapon loadout items in WARDOGS: armor and helmets, tactical vests, backpacks, parachutes, ammo types, sidearms, optics, medical gadgets, throwables and IR gear. It goes deeper than the foundation document and is built so that later diffs against Season 02 are mechanical.

Official Steam posts publish very little item-level data. The official facts are a short list of Season 1 unlock-level and price changes (10 Sep 2026) [1], the rule that throwables cannot be used from enclosed vehicle seats (30 Sep 2026) [2], and the 2 Oct 2026 hotfix that disabled IR Rangefinders in the vendor until Season 02 [3]. Most item-level detail (armor, vests, medical costs, sidearm prices) is player-reported or from beta-era press, and is labelled so.

Confidence is Medium: the changes are official, but the item catalogue rests on player-reported guides and a beta-era press table.

## Armor and helmets

No official armor values exist in the sources found. A guide describes a Level 2 Helmet as protection against sniper fire and body armor as protecting the torso only, with no price or unlock level (player-reported) [5]. The same guide says armor is unlocked via WARDOG Level [5].

## Tactical vests and backpacks

Player-reported: Small Tac Vest opens Quick Slots 5 and 6 with minor reload and equip speed bonuses; Medium opens 5 to 8 with larger bonuses; Large opens all slots [5]. Officially, a Large Backpack and a Sports Parachute exist as Career unlocks at levels 55 and 35 [1]. Small and medium backpack levels are not published.

## Parachutes

Official: Sports Parachute at Career 35 [1]. Player-reported: the Basic Parachute costs $100 and is single-use, lighter than the Sport Parachute [5].

## Ammo types

Official: 762x54mm AP (Career 82) and 556mm AP (Career 83) are unlockable ammo types [1]. Beta press: ammo was billed per caliber, roughly $10 to $250 a box [7]. The per-caliber table is not published.

## Sidearms

Official: Deagle at Career 85 [1]. Beta list prices are in the baseline table [7]; they predate the Season 1 repricing and may be stale.

## Optics and attachments

Official: Recon 6-10x MRAD and MOA scope prices rose 60% and 50% on 10 Sep 2026 [1]. Player-reported: attachments unlock by WARDOG or role level rather than direct purchase [7]; a compact red dot and a 6x Precision Rifle Scope are mentioned without prices [5].

## Medical gadgets and throwables

All figures are player-reported [5] (see baseline table). Official sources confirm only that revive validity is server authoritative (0.1.2) and that grenades, smoke and C4 exist as throwables [2].

## IR gear

IR Rangefinder is described by a boosting-seller blog as thermal goggles or binoculars that make enemies easier to spot (player-reported, conflict of interest) [8]. Price and unlock level are not stated in any source found.

text:
This is a pre-Season-02 baseline of the WARDOGS firearm and launcher roster. Season 02 is announced for 15 October 2026 and the developer says each season has its own XP curve and item order [1][2], so every number here is stamped to Season 1 and expected to change.

Official text names very few weapons. It confirms the Deagle (level 90 reduced to 85), the PP-19 Vityaz 50-round drum magazine (Medic level 33 reduced to 29), 7.62x54mm and 5.56mm armour-piercing ammunition (levels 82 and 83), the starter rifles Bushmaster, A-91 and KH-2002 (named only through camos), rocket launchers in general, and the IR Rangefinders disabled on 2 October 2026 [1][4][9][10]. It publishes no weapon prices, damage or attachment lists. The full roster of 34 firearms and launchers, with prices and unlock levels, comes from press and player-reported guides, which are kept separate from official rows below.

Confidence is Low: the weapon-level numbers rest on guides dated 12 to 17 September 2026 that partly disagree, one of them from a hosting seller.

title: Cash Rewards & Costs
topic: How cash is earned and lost per action, and exploit fixes

text:
Official posts confirm which kinds of action pay cash (revives, transport, kills, spotting, holding the zone), that the Hot Zone pays double cash, and that cash persists between matches [4][5]. They publish no per-action dollar amounts. The only official reward figures found are a temporary 5% end-of-match cash bonus on community servers (14 Sep 2026) and the Season 1 XP-event changes [2][3].

What changed for rewards is documented officially: Update 0.1.2 made revive validity server-authoritative, capped vehicle fly-through rewards, scaled buildable-destruction rewards by build progress and reduced rewards for FOB pallet deposits outside the zone, while a ban policy for economy abuse took effect [1][2]. None of those changes is quantified.

This is a pre-Season-02 baseline (Season 02 is teased for 15 Oct 2026 [7]). Confidence is Medium: the structure of the reward system is official, but amounts are unpublished or rest on player-reported guides.
title: Cash Rewards & Costs
topic: How cash is earned and lost per action, and exploit fixes

text:
- "Every teamplay action you perform rewards cash" and the Hot Zone earns "double the cash" (Steam page, 2026-10-08) [5].
- No official per-action cash amount was found as of 2026-10-08; any figure in a guide is player-reported [4][11].
- Update 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026) capped vehicle fly-through rewards, scaled buildable-destruction rewards to build progress and reduced out-of-zone FOB pallet rewards, with no values stated [1].
- Patch 0.11 (14 Sep 2026) fixed "various cash exploits" and gave community servers a one-week 5% end-of-match cash bonus [2].
- Cash exploit abuse means a timed ban plus cash and XP reset to 0; tutorialising exploits or XP farming means a permanent ban [2]; from 0.1.2 first-offence leniency is over [1].
- Season 1 (10 Sep 2026) changed prices and XP, not documented per-action cash (for example air-vehicle player kill 300 to 250 XP) [3].
- Cash can be exchanged for Gold Bars per an official February 2026 FAQ [4].

text:
## Earning actions

| Source class | Actions listed | Amount |
|--------------|----------------|--------|
| Official (Steam news, 18 Feb 2026) | Revives, transport, kills, spotting, "and MORE" [4] | Not published |
| Official (Steam page) | Reviving squadmates, transporting friendlies to the zone, controlling the objective [5] | Not published |
| Official (0.1.2 notes) | Revive actions, vehicle fly-through, destroying buildables, depositing pallets into a FOB [1] | Not published |
| Player-reported (allthings.how) | Kills, assists, revives, heals, spotting, resupplying, repairing vehicles, FOB building, hauling supplies, driving or flying teammates, standing on the objective, teammate tips, holding the Control Zone, destroying enemy vehicles (loaded helicopters labelled high payout) [11] | Not published |

The player-reported guide's own dollar figures are limited to the $10,000 starting balance [11]. A second guide gives only item costs (for example Galil unlock $35,000, Defibrillator unlock $50,000 plus $1,600 per loadout purchase, Basic Parachute $100), which are costs, not income (player-reported) [12].

## Hot Zone double cash

Official: the Hot Zone is a shifting sub-zone inside the Control Zone, players inside count double for presence and it "yields DOUBLE CASH" [4]. The Steam page repeats "chase the 'Hot Zone' to earn double the cash" [5]. Player-reported: standard cash applies in the Control Zone outside the Hot Zone, and the Hot Zone is a risk-for-payout trade, with no payout figures given [13]. Whether the multiplier applies to every action or only some is not stated officially (see Open Questions).

## Teamplay rewards and what 0.1.2 changed

| Change (30 Sep 2026) | Official wording | Value |
|----------------------|------------------|-------|
| Revive validity | Checks "now fully server authoritative" [1] | n/a |
| Vehicle fly-through | "rewards are now capped" [1] | Cap not stated |
| Destroying buildables | Rewards "scale with their build progress"; a placed schematic no longer gives a full reward [1] | Not stated |
| FOB pallet deposit outside zone | "now awards reduced rewards" [1] | Not stated |

Press coverage (BisectHosting) repeats these points and also states no values (press) [10].

## Exploit and abuse policy

| Offence | Official consequence | Date |
|---------|----------------------|------|
| Abusing cash exploits and bugs | Timed ban scaled to prior bans; cash and XP reset to 0 [2] | 14 Sep 2026 |
| Creating content that tutorialises exploits | Treated as advertising cheats; permanent ban [2] | 14 Sep 2026 |
| XP farming (joining farming servers more than a few minutes) | Permanent ban [2] | 14 Sep 2026 |
| Repeatable unintended exploits, real money trading | Cash and progression reset; risk of permanent ban without warning; first-offence leniency ended [1] | 30 Sep 2026 |

The developer states that testing an exploit "once or twice" is acceptable, but repeating it is abuse [2].

## Season 1 economy changes versus beta

The Season 1.0 changelog (10 Sep 2026) states the previous balance "was designed specifically for weekend long beta tests" and that each season will have a different XP curve and item order [3]. It changes prices and XP, not documented per-action cash. Earning-relevant lines are in the baseline table below; item prices are in price-tables-season-1.

## Income per hour

No sourced income-per-hour figure exists; no official or guide source reviewed gives one. The only quantified pacing statement is that median players at 20 to 25 hours reach about level 20 (XP, not cash) [3].

title: Death Penalty, Loadout Loss & Re-buy
topic: What dying costs, loadout loss, re-buy, insurance-like mechanics, negative balances

text:
The official Steam text fixes the frame of the death penalty but not its size. Every player starts with $10,000, buys a custom loadout "each life", and cash persists from match to match [1]. Bulkhead's own launch-era posts say that "every decision affects YOUR account balance" and that players can min/max their "return on investment every life" [2][3]. No official post, patch note or Q&A in the saved Steam news feed states what is lost on death, what a Re-buy Loadout costs, whether a refund or insurance exists, or what happens at zero cash (checked 2026-10-08) [1][2][3][4][5][6][7].

The detail that does exist is player-reported: an unrevived death forfeits the kit bought for that life, the next kit is paid from the same balance, and a "Re-buy Loadout" vendor option rebuilds the previous kit [9][10]. A vehicle guide says a destroyed vehicle must be paid for again at its spawn price [11]. This document is a pre-Season 02 baseline for diffing against the 15 Oct 2026 update.

Confidence is Low: the answer to the core question (what dying costs) rests entirely on player-reported guides, and none gives a re-buy price.

- Every player starts with $10,000 and, each life, purchases a custom loadout from weapons, gear, utility and vehicles [1].
- Cash persists from match to match, and the store page says spending big on better gear or a vehicle at the right time "could yield massive returns" [1].
- Bulkhead's 21 May 2026 post says "every bullet fired, every loadout built, and every second-to-second choice has real consequences for your account balance" [3].

text:
## Official text: what it does and does not say

| Question | Official answer | Source |
|----------|-----------------|--------|
| Is a loadout bought per life? | Yes: "Each life, you purchase a custom loadout" | [1] |
| Does cash persist between matches? | Yes | [1][2] |
| Is there an exact loss on death? | Not stated | [1][2][3][4][5][6][7] |
| Is there a Re-buy Loadout feature or price? | Not mentioned in any saved official post | [1][2][3][4][5][6][7] |
| Insurance, refunds, grace for low cash? | Not mentioned | [1][2][3][4][5][6][7] |
| Negative balance or zero-cash floor? | Not mentioned | [1][2][3][4][5][6][7] |
| Can cash be spent on anything besides loadouts? | Yes: exchangeable for Gold Bars (cosmetics) | [2] |
| Is there a per-round or seasonal reset? | The Patch 0.11 and 0.1.2 posts say bans reset cash and XP to 0 but state no routine reset; Season 02 notes pending | [6][7] |

The only official text that touches the penalty is framing: stakes are "high" and "every decision" affects the balance [1][3]. A 7 Apr 2026 post adds that a metagame (a Black Market and Vault, and a skills and challenge system) is being built during Early Access, with no economic detail [8].

## Player-reported mechanics

All items in this section are player-reported and not confirmed officially.

| Claim | Source and date | Notes |
|-------|-----------------|-------|
| Unrevived death: "that kit is gone and the next one comes out of the same wallet" | allthings.how, updated 12 Sep 2026 [9] | No dollar figure given |
| Being revived "keeps the loadout you already paid for" | [9] | Consistent with the revive-as-income framing |
| "Re-buy Loadout" rebuilds the previous kit at the vendor | KeenGamer, 17 Sep 2026 [10] | No price stated; whether it costs more than a manual purchase is unknown |
| A helicopter crash "takes your loadout, their loadout, and everyone else in the cabin" | [9] | Wording for pilot and passengers; not tested |
| Repeated deaths can drain reserves | [10] | Qualitative only |
| Destroyed or abandoned vehicle: pay the spawn price again | GameBrief, 17 Sep 2026, figures for the 14 Sep 2026 patch [11] | Repair at a Repair Station with Mechanical Supplies avoids repaying [11] |
| Basic Parachute $100, described as inexpensive insurance against losing a loadout in a damaged aircraft | [10] | Not an actual insurance mechanic |
| Emergency Resuscitator free, usable once per life | [10] | Not tested |
| Defibrillator $1,600 when bought for a loadout | [10] | Also in combat-loadouts-foundation |

## Low and zero cash

No source describes what the game does when the balance cannot cover a loadout, whether a minimal free kit exists, or whether the balance can go negative. The allthings.how guide notes only that there is "no per-round reset to bail you out" and advises checking the balance before each rebuy [9]. The KeenGamer guide advises not building a loadout so expensive that "several deaths destroy your cash reserves" [10]. Neither describes a floor (player-reported). Two other facts bear indirectly: Bulkhead resets cash and XP to 0 as an anti-exploit penalty, which implies zero is a valid state [6][7], and the Emergency Resuscitator is reported free [10].

## Vehicle loss costs

Vehicles are bought per life at a spawn price (player-reported) [11]. Official Season 1 changelog prices for vehicle-class items are below [5]. The changelog does not say whether each figure is a one-time unlock payment or the recurring per-life price, so the repayment cost after a loss cannot be derived from official text alone (see Open Questions).

text:
WARDOGS runs a persistent cash economy. Every player starts with $10,000, team-play actions earn cash, cash carries from match to match, and each life the player buys a loadout of weapons, gear, utility and vehicles [1][5]. Bulkhead states that in-game cash and Gold Bars "must be earned through play" and will never be sold for real money [6][10]. Cash can also be exchanged for Gold Bars, the "endgame currency" for cosmetic unlocks in the Gold Market [5]. The UK Steam price is £36.99 (Standard), with a £45.99 Supporter Edition and a £11.99 Supporter Pack DLC that is cosmetic only [1][10].

This revision reads the full official Steam posts, which are now in the local snapshot. They give an exact vendor and vehicle price-change list for Season 1 (10 Sep 2026) [4], the Patch 0.11 economy abuse policy [3] and the Update 0.1.2 reward fixes [2], none with per-action cash amounts. Two areas are still not settled by official text: the death penalty and re-buy rule (player-reported only), and the season-end cash and XP wipe with automatic Gold Bar conversion (press and player-reported, traced to a 7 Apr 2026 devlog video that is not in any Steam post). Depth is in the linked economy documents.

Document confidence is Medium: the loop, prices and monetisation are official, but the death penalty and seasonal wipe are unverified, so the document cannot be rated higher while they stay open.

text:
- **Cash**: the in-game currency earned and spent in matches, held in the account balance; never sold for real money [1][6].
- **Account balance**: the persistent cash total that outcomes feed into [1][12].
- **Loadout**: weapons, gear, utility and vehicles bought each life [1].
- **Track / Career / Driver / Pilot**: progression tracks that gate unlocks by level; unlock gates are separate from cash prices [4].

- **Gold Market**: the store for cosmetic unlocks bought with Gold Bars [5].

text:
All facts below are for Early Access, as of 2026-10-08.

- Starting balance is $10,000 [1].
- Every teamplay action rewards cash, the Hot Zone yields double cash, and cash persists between matches [1][5].
- Each life, the player buys a custom loadout of weapons, gear, utility and vehicles [1][5].
- Cash can be exchanged for Gold Bars, used for cosmetic unlocks in the Gold Market (18 Feb 2026 FAQ; not restated in later posts) [5].
- Bulkhead states: no monetization during Early Access apart from the optional Supporter Edition; cash and Gold Bars must be earned through play; camos cannot be bought directly [6][10].
- Steam lists Standard at £36.99, Supporter Edition at £45.99 and the Supporter Pack DLC at £11.99; the DLC contains cosmetics only (see editions-pricing-platforms) [1][10].
- The Steam page says the team plans lower Early Access pricing and may raise it nearer full release; Early Access is expected to last around 1 to 2 years [1].
- The latest posted version is Update 0.1.2 (30 Sep) [2]; two official posts on 2 Oct covered a security and stability hotfix notice and an IR Rangefinder and CIWS balance hotfix [8][9]; Season 02 is teased for 15 Oct 2026 [7].
title: Economy: Foundation
topic: Account balance, costs, rewards, death penalty

text:
## Earning cash

Official sources confirm which actions pay (revives, transport, kills, spotting, "and MORE") and that the Hot Zone yields double cash [5], but publish no per-action dollar amounts. The only official reward figure is a one-week 5% community-server end-of-match cash bonus from 14 Sep 2026 [3]. Update 0.1.2 made revive checks server authoritative, capped vehicle fly-through rewards, scaled buildable-destruction rewards with build progress (a placed schematic no longer pays in full) and reduced pallet-deposit rewards outside a FOB zone, with no values stated [2]. Community guides add income sources and no amounts (player-reported) [15]. See cash-rewards-and-costs.

## Spending cash

Cash buys the per-life loadout [1]. The Season 1 launch changelog (post of 9 Sep 2026, Season 1.0 live 10 Sep) lists these official price changes [4]:

| Item | Old | New |
|------|-----|-----|
| Forward Operating Base (vendor) | $2,500 | $7,500 |
| Large Hammer (vendor) | $1,600 | $2,400 |
| Support Medium Hammer | $10,000 | $25,000 |
| Support Large Hammer | $25,000 | $75,000 |
| Career Artillery Tank | $400,000 | $500,000 |
| Pilot Little Bird with miniguns | $25,000 | $50,000 |
| Pilot Z20 Lakota | $50,000 | $35,000 |
| Driver URAL | $50,000 | $35,000 |
| Driver Dune Buggy | $35,000 | $25,000 |
| Driver Kodiak Flatbed | $15,000 | $35,000 |

The same list also moves scope, small supply crate and Music Tape H prices and rescales the supply-crate purchase curve from 25 to 250 down to 1 to 200 [4]. The Kodiak Flatbed is an official increase, and its unlock level moved from 2 to 10 [4]; the full table is in price-tables-season-1. The changelog does not say whether a price is a one-time unlock payment or a per-life price.

Per-spawn vehicle prices (for example $500 for a Bobcat, about $8,000 for the SPH-2, about $18,000 for the Havoc) are community measurements, not an official table (player-reported) [16].

## Death penalty

Official pages say a loadout is bought each life and that outcomes feed the balance [1][12], but no official post states the loss on death, any re-buy price, refund or zero-cash rule (all saved official posts checked). Community guides report that a downed player who is not revived loses the kit bought for that life, the next kit is paid from the same balance, and a helicopter crash can destroy pilot and passenger loadouts (player-reported) [15][16]. See death-penalty-and-rebuy.

## Currencies, persistence and seasons

Cash persists between matches and can be exchanged for Gold Bars [5]. Each season will have "a different XP curve with different item orders" [4]. Official: bans for cash exploits reset an offender's cash and XP to 0 [3]. Not in any official post: that every player's cash and XP reset at season end and that leftover cash converts automatically to Gold Bars. This is relayed by press and a seller from a 7 Apr 2026 devlog video, not by the Steam post of that date, which only announces the planned Metagame (Black Market, Vault, skills and challenges) [11][17] (press and player-reported). The conversion rate is unpublished. See season-reset-and-currencies.

## Monetization

| Product | Price (Steam, 2026-10-08) |
|---------|---------------------------|
| WARDOGS | £36.99 [1] |
| Supporter Edition | £45.99 [1] |
| Supporter Pack (DLC) | £11.99 [1][10] |

The Supporter Pack holds three Starter Weapon camos (Valkyra A-91, Lonestar Bushmaster, Manticore KH-2002), a Littlebird "Taxi" camo, a hideable scoreboard supporter icon and two bobbleheads; no gameplay item is listed [10][6]. The launch press release quoted $39.99 USD for Early Access [12]; the 11 Aug post refers to "stair stepped pricing" without figures [6]. Regional prices are in editions-pricing-platforms.

This is the pre-Season-02 baseline of every price the studio itself has published for WARDOGS. Season 02 is due 15 Oct 2026 and the studio says each season gets a different XP curve and item order [1], so these values are expected to be superseded.

Confidence is High because every value is quoted from an official Steam post or the Steam store data; no player-reported figures are used.

text:
This is the pre-wipe baseline for seasons and currencies, taken on 2026-10-08, one week before Season 02 (15 October 2026). Official Steam posts confirm that cash persists from match to match, that cash can be exchanged for Gold Bars, that Gold Bars are the "endgame currency" for cosmetic unlocks in a "Gold Market", that Gold Bars and cash will never be sold for real money, and that each season gets its own XP curve and item order [2][3][4]. The Season 02 teaser confirms only the date [1].

The explicit rule that a season end resets cash and XP, auto-converts leftover cash to Gold Bars, and keeps Gold Bars and cosmetics permanently is NOT in any Steam post in the local snapshot. It is attributed to a 7 April 2026 BULKHEAD devlog and is relayed by Vice, KeenGamer and Timesaver.gg [10][11][12]. The earlier single-source Timesaver claim is therefore half-confirmed: the existence of Gold Bars and the cash-to-Gold exchange are officially confirmed; the automatic end-of-season conversion and permanence rest on a devlog the press quotes but this KB could not read. The conversion rate is unpublished everywhere.

Confidence is Medium: the currency model is official, the wipe mechanics are second-hand.

text:
- **Season**: a content and progression cycle; "Season 1.0" is the label for the 10 Sep 2026 launch changelog [4].
- **Cash**: persistent in-game currency, earned by teamplay and spent on loadouts [2][9].
- **Gold Bars**: the "endgame currency" obtained by exchanging cash, spent on cosmetics [2].
- **Gold Market**: the named store for cosmetic unlocks bought with Gold Bars [2].
- **Wipe / reset**: loss of cash and XP progression; in this KB "seasonal reset" is the press-reported end-of-season event, distinct from the exploit-sanction reset [5][10].

As of 2026-10-08, pre-wipe:

- Season 1 is live (build 0.1.2 plus hotfixes); Season 02 is teased for 15 October 2026 [1][5][8].
- Cash persists between matches [2][9].
- Cash can be exchanged for Gold Bars; Gold Bars buy cosmetics in the Gold Market [2].
- Neither cash nor Gold Bars is ever to be sold, and camos are not to be purchasable directly [3].
- The only real-money item is the optional Supporter Edition (cosmetics) [3][9].
- The studio frames progression as "continue earning, progressing and adding value to your account even when not in a match" via a planned Metagame, including a Black Market and Vault and a Skills and Challenge system, built during Early Access [7].
- The 22 Sep teaser contains only "WARDOGS Season 02 is coming. 15th October 2026. Stay tuned for more details." [1]
- The 30 Sep post promised more information "next week" [5]; no further official Season 02 post existed in the snapshot at 2026-10-08.

## Gold Bars: the Timesaver claim

Timesaver.gg claims leftover cash converts to Gold Bars and that Gold Bars and cosmetics are "the only things that survive" the wipe, and sells in-game cash [12]. Assessment: partly confirmed, confidence Medium. The Gold Bar currency, the cash exchange and the cosmetic role are in an official Steam post [2], and Vice and KeenGamer independently relay the same end-of-season rule [10][11]. The part still without a readable official text is the automatic conversion and permanence; Timesaver cites the 7 April devlog for it [12]. The official 7 April Steam post only announces the Metagame and links a video [7]. Timesaver also has a commercial interest in cash, so its "spend first" advice and rate remarks are not evidence.

Rain: Vice reports BULKHEAD said on X that rain is an additional per-map weather state, not a dynamic mid-match event [10]. Not economy, noted because it travels with the same reset coverage.

| Cash balance | Resets; converts to Gold Bars | [10][11] |

| Role-track unlocks | Follow level; order may change per season | [4][10] |
| Gold Bars | Persist | [10][11] |
| Cosmetics bought with Gold Bars | Persist ("intended to remain") | [10][11] |
| Supporter Edition cosmetics | Not stated; they are sold items, not season rewards | [3] |

text:
The official sources describe the match loop in a few sentences: three teams contest a randomised 2x2 km Control Zone inside a 256 km2 map, the team with the most players inside earns points, and the first to 100 points wins [1][2]. A Hot Zone is a shifting sub-zone inside the Control Zone where each player counts double towards the player count and cash is doubled [2]. That is the whole of the officially published scoring rule at Season 01.

Everything finer-grained is player-reported: the 30-second scoring tick, one point per tick, the tower and code mechanic that drags the Hot Zone, the deployment board, the APC spawn and its cooldown [12][13]. No official source published at 2026-10-08 states respawn timers, spawn placement rules, team-balance rules or match length. This document records those gaps explicitly as a baseline so Season 02 changes can be diffed.

Confidence is Medium. The core rule rests on the Steam page and the developer's Top Questions post; spawn, tick and tower detail rests on player-reported guides, which may not raise a claim above Medium.

Verified 2026-10-08 against the sources shown.

- Up to 100 players in three teams fight over one Control Zone [1][2]. Official team names are Lonestar, Valkyra and Manticore (18 Feb 2026) [2].
- The Control Zone is a randomised 2x2 km area within a 256 km2 map; zone location varies per match [2].
- The team with the most players in the zone earns points; the first team to 100 points wins [1][2].
- The Hot Zone is a shifting sub-zone; players count double towards player count and it pays double cash [2].
- Players start with $10,000 and buy a loadout each life; cash persists between matches [1][2].
- Squad size is unlimited; squads get extra UI, communication tools and vehicle locking [2].
- Proximity chat is confirmed by the developer; the store page calls it local voice chat [1][2].
- Patch 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026): revive validity checks are now fully server authoritative, vehicle fly-through rewards are capped, buildable-destruction rewards scale with build progress, and depositing pallets into a FOB outside the zone pays reduced rewards [7].
- 2 Oct 2026 balance hotfix: IR Rangefinders disabled in the vendor until Season 02 (where they will require batteries); the CIWS destroys the Havoc in about 6 seconds instead of 12 [8].
- Season 02 is dated 15 Oct 2026 and is described as a larger update with new map conditions, equipment, balance reworks and additional features [7][9].

text:
## Baseline values

All values are as of Season 01, 0.1.2 plus 2 Oct 2026 hotfixes, unless a different date is shown. "Official" means developer-published; "PR" means player-reported.

| Value | As-of version | Source |
|-------|---------------|--------|
| Max players per match: 100 | Season 01 (store page, 18 Feb 2026 post) | Official [1][2] |
| Teams: 3 (Lonestar, Valkyra, Manticore) | Season 01 | Official [2] |
| Win threshold: 100 points | Season 01 | Official [1][2] |
| Control Zone size: 2x2 km, randomised | Season 01 | Official [1][2] |
| Map size: 256 km2 | 18 Feb 2026 post | Official [2] |
| Hot Zone presence weight: x2 per player | 18 Feb 2026 post | Official [2] |
| Hot Zone cash multiplier: x2 | 18 Feb 2026 post | Official [2] |
| Starting cash: $10,000 | Season 01 | Official [1] |
| Squad size: unlimited | 18 Feb 2026 post | Official [2] |
| Scoring tick: 30 s, 1 point to leader | Guide read Oct 2026 | PR [12][13] |
| Players per team: about 33 | Guide read Oct 2026 | PR [13] |
| Capture towers per Control Zone: 3 to 5 | Guide read Oct 2026 | PR [13] |
| Drill rig activation: 6,000 fuel | Guide read Oct 2026 | PR [13] |
| Zone occupation pay: $160 (Control Zone), $320 (Hot Zone) per cycle | Guide read Oct 2026 | PR [13] |
| M113 APC unlock: any faction at 20 points | Guide read Oct 2026 | PR [13] |
| APC spawn personal cooldown: 10 minutes | Guide read Oct 2026 | PR [13] |
| New Recruit discount: 50% until account level 9 | Guide read Oct 2026 | PR [13] |
| Match length: can exceed 1 hour | Guide read Oct 2026 | PR [13] |
| CIWS time to destroy Havoc: about 6 s (was 12 s) | 2 Oct 2026 hotfix | Official [8] |
| IR Rangefinder: disabled in vendor until Season 02 | 2 Oct 2026 hotfix | Official [8] |
| Community-server end-of-match cash bonus: 5% for one week | 0.11, 14 Sep 2026 (expired) | Official [6] |
| Season 02 date: 15 Oct 2026 | Teaser 22 Sep 2026 | Official [9] |

## Match lifecycle

| Stage | What is known | Class |
|-------|---------------|-------|
| 1. Find a server | From 0.1.2, Deploy offers Official, Community, Infantry Mode and Low-Level lists; the browsers were split into Official and Community in 0.11; a queue position is shown after Join [6][7] | Official |
| 2. Spawn and buy | Buy a loadout each life at the Equipment Vendor in the Safe Zone, then spawn through the deployment board; "Rebuy Last Loadout" restores the previous kit [1][12][13] | Store page official; interface detail PR |
| 3. Reach the zone | Transporting friendlies to the zone earns cash; ground vehicles and helicopters carry players [1][13] | Official / PR |
| 4. Contest | The team with most players in the zone earns points; Hot Zone doubles presence [1][2] | Official |
| 5. End | First team to 100 points wins [1][2] | Official |

Not published officially: what happens after a win (map rotation, scoreboard, lobby return), match-length targets and round time limits. Assessment: the lifecycle after step 5 cannot be described from sources; confidence Low.

## Control Zone and scoring

Officially, scoring is a comparison of player counts inside the zone, awarding points to the leader, to a threshold of 100 [1][2]. The official text does not say how often points are awarded, whether a tie awards points, or whether the margin matters. One player-reported guide gives a 30-second check with one point to the leading team, which implies a minimum of about 50 minutes (100 checks) if a team leads every check [13]. Assessment: that figure is arithmetic on a player-reported tick, not a measured match length; confidence Low. The same guide says matches can pass an hour [13].

## Hot Zone

Official: a shifting sub-zone within the Control Zone; players count as double towards player count, "leading to match-swinging potential", and it yields double cash [2]. The store page repeats "chase the Hot Zone to earn double the cash" [1].

Player-reported: it appears as a yellow sub-zone on the tactical map with a circular minimap outline; size and relocation interval are not published [12]. A second guide describes a drifting circle that can be pulled toward a tower by entering a master code, and toward a player FOB by a fuel-fed drill rig [13]. These tower and rig mechanics are not described in any official post read for this document.

## Three-team dynamics

The developer designed three teams so that the zone is a three-way contest, with a lore split: Lonestar (Western paramilitary), Valkyra (Soviet-revival) and Manticore (Persian shadow army) [2]. Because points go to the team with the most players, a team can lead while outnumbered by the other two combined; this follows from the rule as stated and is an inference (Assessment: confidence Medium; basis: the scoring rule at [2]). No official source states how players are assigned to teams, whether teams are balanced to equal size, or whether team switching is restricted. The 0.11 post lists "Team Switching Controls" and "AFK kicking during seeding disabling" as upcoming features, which implies team switching and seeding phases exist but were not yet adequately controlled on 12 Sep 2026 [6]. A player-reported guide gives about 33 players per team [13].

## Spawn, respawn and deploy

- Official: the 0.1.2 Deploy flow is a pre-match server selection screen aimed at steering players to Infantry Mode and Low-Level servers [7].
- Official: revive validity checks are server authoritative from 0.1.2 [7].
- Player-reported: loadout purchase at the Equipment Vendor, then spawn via the deployment board [12].
- Player-reported: there is no squad spawning; an M113 APC unlocks once any faction reaches 20 points, the deployment computer can teleport you to an allied APC with a 10-minute personal cooldown, and destroying an APC's satellite dish disables its spawn function [13].
- Player-reported: reviving is cheaper than respawning [13]. Revive duration is not given [12].
- Not published: respawn timer, spawn point distribution, spawn protection, spawn-camping rules.

## Developer statements on intended tactical play

The "Tactical Depth & Teamplay" post (21 May 2026) gives three bullets: real-world ballistics, audio and flight models; every decision affects your account balance; a 100% player-driven militaristic sandbox. It frames a Debrief video on three pillars of tactical depth [4]. The post text names no mechanic more specific than that; the video content is not transcribed in the snapshot. Related official statements elsewhere:

- "Teamplay isn't encouraged, it's rewarded": revives, transport, kills, spotting and more pay cash in the zone [2].
- Roles are player-defined by purchased gear, earning XP across six tracks [2].
- "There are no set rules of engagement"; examples include chasing the Hot Zone, sniping in a ghillie suit, helicopter supply runs, building a forward operating base at a chokepoint, and artillery tanks [1].
- The mode was developed with the original ARMA King of the Hill mod creators as a standalone KOTH-inspired shooter [3].
- A 16 Jun 2026 devlog says the line between arcade and realistic has been drawn by the developer, without stating mechanics [5].

text:
WARDOGS is a 100-player, three-team tactical shooter in Steam Early Access since 10 September 2026 [1][2]. Its core mode is the Control Zone: three teams contest a randomised 2x2 km zone inside a 256 km2 map, the team with the most players inside earns points, and the first to 100 points wins [1][2]. A shifting Hot Zone inside it counts each player double and pays double cash [2]. Proximity or local voice chat is part of the design [1][2].

Progression is cash-based, with cash persisting from match to match and exchangeable for Gold Bars, plus XP across six role tracks (Career, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver, Pilot) that gate unlocks [2][3]. The developer states that each season gets a different XP curve and item order [3]. Season 02 is dated 15 October 2026 and described only as a larger content update; the official text says nothing about a wipe or rain [5][8].

Confidence is High for the core claims, which now rest on the store page, the Top Questions post and the Season 1 changelog, the 0.11 and 0.1.2 posts and the two 2 Oct posts. Level caps, scoring tick, tower mechanics and the Season 02 wipe are not in official text and are kept as player-reported or press-reported.

- Hot Zone: a shifting sub-zone where players count as double and cash is doubled [2].
- Voice: the store page says local voice chat and the developer FAQ says proximity chat [1][2]; the claim that it carries across all three teams rests on the Team17 press release [12].
- Progression: cash persists between matches and can be exchanged for Gold Bars [2]; XP accrues across six role tracks named Career, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver and Pilot [3].
- Seasons: each season has its own XP curve and item order [3]; Season 02 is dated 15 Oct 2026 [8]. Official text states no wipe; a progression wipe is press-reported only [13].
- Modes: the Control Zone is the only named core mode; Official servers run no modified modes, while Community servers can; since 0.1.2 a Deploy flow offers Official, Community, Infantry Mode and Low-Level servers [4][5].
- 1.0: no date; the 7 Apr 2026 post commits to building a metagame (Black Market and Vault, Player Skills and Challenge System) during Early Access [10].

text:
All statements verified 2026-10-08 against the sources shown.

- Early Access began 10 Sep 2026; the developer describes it as fully playable and representing the core vision [2]. Setting is the war-torn region of Kolchia [2].
- Matches support up to 100 players split across three rival teams on a 256 km2 map; squad size is unlimited [2].
- Teams fight for a randomised 2x2 km Control Zone; the team with the most players in the zone earns points and the first to 100 wins [1][2].
- The Hot Zone counts players double and yields double cash [2].
- Every player starts with $10,000 and buys a loadout each life; teamplay actions such as reviving, transporting friendlies and controlling the objective earn cash; cash persists between matches [1].
- Cash can be exchanged for Gold Bars, used for cosmetics in the Gold Market; the developer says cash and Gold Bars will never be sold for real money [2][9].
- Voice: the store page lists local voice chat; the FAQ says proximity chat, including loudspeakers players can construct [1][2].
- Launch content is three maps, each with three variations, with infantry and vehicle combat [12].
- The Season 1 changelog (9 Sep 2026, pre-load) slowed the XP curve and moved unlocks; it also fixed voice dropping after a failed join, push-to-talk targeting and re-login recovery, and added a visible communication status [3].
- Patch 0.11 (14 Sep 2026) split the server browser into Official and Community lists, removed filters from the Official list, and gave Community servers a 5% end-of-match cash bonus for one week [4].
- Patch 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026) made revive checks server authoritative, capped fly-through rewards, scaled buildable-destruction rewards by build progress, reduced rewards for FOB pallet deposits outside the zone, added the Deploy flow, and added Advanced Filters back to the Official list [5].
- 2 Oct 2026 brought two official posts: a security and stability hotfix at 08:00 UTC with no gameplay detail, and a balance hotfix disabling IR Rangefinders in the vendor until Season 02 (where they will need batteries) and cutting the CIWS kill time on the Havoc from about 12 s to about 6 s [6][7].
- Season 02 is dated 15 Oct 2026 by the official teaser of 22 Sep 2026; the 0.1.2 post calls it a larger content update with new map conditions, equipment, balance reworks and additional features [5][8].

| Role tracks | Six: Career, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver, Pilot | [2][3] |
| Track cap | Level 100 per track and account level to 600: player-reported only; no official cap | [15] |
| Unlock cost | Reaching a level makes an item buyable; the changelog moves items between levels and tracks | [3] |
| Per-season curve | "Each season we will have a different XP curve with different item orders" | [3] |
| Season reset | Not stated in official text; press reports cash and XP reset with leftover cash converted to Gold Bars | [13] |

The official Season 1 changelog slowed levels around 10 to 20 and flattened the curve from level 35: level 10 rose from 25,000 to 35,000 XP, level 15 from 54,750 to 110,000, level 20 from 111,500 to 250,000 and level 50 from 838,000 to 1,000,000; an air-vehicle player kill pays 250 XP, down from 300 [3]. The developer targets a median player at 20 to 25 hours being around level 20 [3]. The official name "Career" is used in the changelog; "Assault" is a player-guide name [3][15]. Economy abuse penalties (timed ban with cash and XP reset to 0; permanent ban for exploit tutorials and XP farming) are official from 0.11 and were reaffirmed in 0.1.2 [4][5]. Full tables are in progression-and-role-tracks, progression-unlock-tables and season-reset-and-currencies.

## Modes available at Early Access

The only core mode named in official text is the Control Zone [1][2]. Official servers do not run modified game modes, while Community servers can [4]. The 0.1.2 Deploy flow lets players choose Official, Community, Infantry Mode or Low-Level servers, described as a first step to signpost servers running these modifiers; the post does not define the rules of either modifier [5]. Assessment: a full catalogue of community-server modes is unavailable; confidence Low.

## Planned for 1.0

The 7 Apr 2026 post says the Metagame (the frontend experience to keep earning and progressing outside a match) is designed and will be built throughout Early Access, including the Black Market and Vault and a Player Skills and Challenge System [10]. The more detailed store-page list (more maps, weapons and vehicles, deeper progression, fighter jets, around one to two years of Early Access) is not in the saved store JSON and is cited to the live store page and Team17 press release only; re-verify before relying on it [1][12]. A third-party roadmap article adds new objective types and says no dated roadmap will be published, but does not say which items are official [14].

text:
This document is a pre-Season 02 baseline of WARDOGS progression: the role-track XP curve, XP event values, the unlock-level moves, the 0.1.2 exploit fixes and what is officially said about seasons. It is written from the full text of the official Steam posts saved in the 2026-10-08 snapshot, which supersede the press summaries used in the foundation documents.

The official Season 1 changelog (posted 9 Sep 2026) names six role tracks: Career, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver and Pilot [1]. It gives an XP band table from level 6 to level 50 (level 50 costs 1,000,000 XP), says the old values were tuned for weekend-long beta tests, and says each season will have a different XP curve and item order [1]. The Season 02 teaser contains only a date, 15 October 2026, and says nothing about XP [3]. The official posts do not state a level cap or any WARDOG level; those come from a player-reported guide [9].

Confidence is Medium. The XP bands, event values and unlock moves rest on an official post (High on their own). The level cap, the WARDOG level formula and the seasonal wipe details rest on player-reported or press sources, which holds the document at Medium.

text:
## Role tracks and the 4-versus-6 and naming conflicts

| Question | Official text | Other sources | Resolution |
|----------|---------------|---------------|------------|
| How many tracks? | Six names appear: Career, Medic, Recon, Support, Driver, Pilot [1] | Six tracks, four levelled by weapons and tools, Driver and Pilot levelled by vehicles (player-reported) [9] | Six. The "four" is a count of weapon-based tracks, not a smaller set. |
| What is the first track called? | "Career" [1] | "Assault", levelled from assault rifles (player-reported) [9] | Official wording is Career. Whether Career is a rename of, or the same track as, the guide's Assault is not stated in the official post. Open question. |
| Does an official post call the tracks "roles"? | It says "role track" [1] | Guides say "roles" [9] | Use "role track". |

Evidence that Career is a full track and not a catch-all: the changelog lists Career unlocks (Sports Parachute, Large Backpack, 762x54mm AP, 556mm AP, Deagle, Artillery Tank) [1]. The changelog also records items moving between tracks: Music Tape H from Pilot to Driver, and Heavy Tank from Career to Driver [1].

## XP sources named in official text

| Source | Value | Source of value |
|--------|-------|-----------------|
| Player kill using an air vehicle | 250 XP (was 300) | [1] |
| Supply crate item sold under $75 | 1 XP (was 25) | [1] |
| Revives | Validity now server authoritative (value not published) | [2] |
| Destroying buildables | Reward scales with build progress; a placed schematic no longer gives full reward (value not published) | [2] |
| Vehicle fly-through | Rewards capped (cap not published) | [2] |
| FOB pallet deposit outside the zone | Reduced reward (value not published) | [2] |

Other XP sources (kills, objectives, spotting) are described only in guides; the guide says Driver XP comes from "kills and objectives from a ground vehicle" and Pilot XP from flying helicopters (player-reported) [9].

## Season 1 curve versus beta

The changelog says the earlier balancing "was designed specifically for weekend long beta tests" and that the new values are "in-line with where we believe they should be" [1]. The "old" column below is therefore the beta-era curve, as stated by the developer.

| Level | Beta XP | Season 1 XP | Change as published | Derived: Season 1 XP added since previous band |
|-------|---------|-------------|---------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Below 6 | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged | n/a |
| 6 | 8,750 | 9,250 | 5.7% slower | n/a |
| 10 | 25,000 | 35,000 | 40.0% slower | 25,750 |
| 15 | 54,750 | 110,000 | 100.9% slower | 75,000 |
| 20 | 111,500 | 250,000 | 124.2% slower | 140,000 |
| 25 | 192,000 | 325,000 | 69.3% slower | 75,000 |
| 30 | 293,750 | 400,000 | 36.2% slower | 75,000 |
| 35 | 416,500 | 500,000 | 20.0% slower | 100,000 |
| 40 | 551,250 | 650,000 | 17.9% slower | 150,000 |
| 45 | 689,500 | 800,000 | 16.0% slower | 150,000 |
| 50 | 838,000 | 1,000,000 | 19.3% slower | 200,000 |

Source for the first four data columns: [1]. The last column is my subtraction of adjacent Season 1 values and is not in any source. Assessment: the headline says the slowdown is "around 10 to 20" with flattening from 35 onward, yet the published bands show every band to level 50 slower than beta by at least 16 percent; confidence High that this is what the table says, Low on what the developer meant by "flatten" (the post does not elaborate) [1]. The same section describes "a larger increase at level 10" than the 5.7 percent at level 6 [1].

Intermediate levels (for example 7 to 9, 11 to 14) have no published XP value; the post gives bands only [1]. Whether the figures are cumulative per track or per level is not spelled out; the XP-to-reach wording ("Level 10: 25,000 to 35,000") reads as cumulative requirement (Assessment: Medium confidence, based on the figures rising monotonically) [1].

## Level caps and WARDOG level

- Official: no level cap is stated. The highest levels named in the changelog are Career level 90 (Artillery Tank) and Career level 85 (Deagle), so a cap of at least 90 is implied (Assessment: High that the cap is 90 or more, from [1]).
- Player-reported: each track caps at level 100, and the account-wide WARDOG Level is "the sum of all six tracks" capped at 600 [9]. The arithmetic (6 x 100 = 600) is consistent with a cap of 100, but neither number is in an official post I read.
- Official XP stops at level 50 (1,000,000 XP); XP needed for levels 51 to 100 is not published [1].

## How Season 1 changed progression versus beta

| Area | Beta | Season 1 | Source |
|------|------|----------|--------|
| XP design target | Tuned for weekend-long tests | Tuned for long-term play; per-season curves | [1] |
| XP curve | See table above | Slowed at every published band from level 6 | [1] |
| Air vehicle kill XP | 300 | 250 | [1] |
| Low-value supply crate sale XP | 25 | 1 | [1] |
| Supply crate purchase curve | 25 to 250 | 1 to 200 ("rescaled") | [1] |
| Items per track | Many items at earlier levels | Many moved (see below) | [1] |

Baseline of unlock-level moves in the Season 1 changelog (full tables belong to progression-unlock-tables) [1]:

| Track | Item | Old level | Season 1 level |
|-------|------|-----------|----------------|
| Career | Sports Parachute | 36 | 35 |
| Career | Large Backpack | 56 | 55 |
| Career | 762x54mm AP | 83 | 82 |
| Career | 556mm AP | 85 | 83 |
| Career | Deagle | 90 | 85 |

| Medic | PP-19 50 round drum magazine | 33 | 29 |
| Support | Large Hammer | 7 | 8 |

| Driver | URAL Attack | 40 | 25 |

## 0.1.2 XP and cash exploit fixes (30 Sep 2026)

All from the official 0.1.2 post [2]:

1. Revive action validity checks are fully server authoritative.
2. Vehicle fly-through exploit fixed; rewards capped.
3. Rewards for destroying buildables scale with build progress.
4. Depositing pallets into a FOB outside the zone awards reduced rewards.
5. Policy: anyone caught abusing cash and XP exploits or Real Money Trading "has had their cash and progression reset and risks being permanently banned"; first-time leniency is over; repeatable unintended exploits can bring a permanent ban without warning [2].

The earlier patch 0.11 post (12 Sep 2026) set the tiers: cash exploits get a timed ban and a cash and XP reset to 0; tutorials on exploits count as advertising cheats and get a permanent ban; XP farming "will result in the most serious bans" and joining a known XP-farming server for more than a few minutes risks a permanent ban [4]. The post gives no figure for the reduced or capped rewards [2].

## What the Season 02 teaser says about XP

The official teaser (22 Sep 2026) reads, in full, that Season 02 is coming, dated 15 October 2026, with "more details" to follow, plus a trailer link [3]. It says nothing about XP, levels or resets. What is known about XP in Season 02 comes from elsewhere:

- Official, indirect: "Each season we will have a different XP curve with different item orders" (Season 1 changelog) [1]. Season 02 is "a larger content update, with new map conditions, equipment, balance reworks and additional features" [2].
- Press: Vice (23 Sep 2026) says players "should expect a progression wipe", that Bulkhead "has previously explained that cash and level progression reset at the end of a season", that leftover cash converts to Gold Bars and that Gold Bars and cosmetics persist; it also says the new unlock order and conversion rate are not yet shared [8].
- Player-reported: a guide says WARDOG Level and cash "drop to zero" when a major update cycle ends [9].

text:
This depth document goes beyond maps-environment-foundation on how WARDOGS describes its destruction, its level design and its map scale, using the full text of Bulkhead's official Steam posts saved locally on 2026-10-08. It is a pre-Season-02 baseline: Season 02 is dated 15 Oct 2026 and a progression wipe is expected, so every number below is stamped with the version it applies to.

The headline finding is that the official "Level Design & Performance" devlog (16 Jul 2026) is a short video post. Its text says nothing about map size, map count, destruction rules or the "sandbox" term; it only says the team gathered references "firsthand in Georgia", optimised across a wide range of hardware, and offers graphics options [3]. The map-size and sandbox questions are answered by other official text. An 18 Feb 2026 Bulkhead post states that the Control Zone is a randomised 2x2 km area "within a large-scale 256km² map" [2]. This contradicts the frozen foundation, which treats 256 km² as a third-party figure only (see Open Questions). The Steam store page calls the game a "large-scale, up to 100-player militaristic sandbox" with "building and destruction mechanics" and "larger maps" [1]. The "3 maps x 3 variations" count appears only in the Team17 press release as quoted by the foundation [9].

Confidence is Medium. The scale, sandbox and destruction claims rest on official Bulkhead text, but no official source describes the destruction model, terrain deformation, persistence or the performance cost of destruction, and the Season 02 rain details are press-reported.

text:
- Official text resolves "sandbox": the Steam page and Bulkhead's posts use it for the player-driven, build-and-destroy play space ("a large-scale, up to 100-player militaristic sandbox", "100% player-driven militaristic sandbox"), not for a map type [1][4][5]. It does not conflict with a fixed roster of maps (Season 01) [1][9].
- Official text states a 256 km² map and a randomised 2x2 km Control Zone inside it, in a Bulkhead post of 18 Feb 2026 (pre-release) [2]. The Steam page itself says only "larger maps" and gives no total size [1].
- A 256 km² area is 16 km x 16 km if square, which matches the community "about 16 km edge to edge" claim arithmetically; the official text does not state the shape [2][13].
- The official destruction statements are: a "destructible battlefield" [1], rocket launchers can destroy apartment blocks [1], and "the world around you reacts to your presence" [1]. Nothing official says terrain is deformable or that damage persists across matches.
- The "Level Design & Performance" post is about performance, not destruction rules: Georgian reference gathering, hardware optimisation, and graphics options [3]. Bulkhead says the engine is UE5 enhanced by a custom "WAR DYNAMICS FRAMEWORK" for 100-player density [2].
- Patch 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026) made destroying buildables scale with build progress, so a placed schematic no longer pays a full reward [7].
- Season 02 (15 Oct 2026) is officially "a larger content update, with new map conditions" [7][8]. The rain-as-per-map-state detail is press-reported only [10][11].

text:
## Settling "sandbox" versus "3 maps x 3 variations"

| Question | Official answer | Source |
|----------|-----------------|--------|
| What does "sandbox" mean? | Player-driven play space with build and destroy freedom; "100% player-driven militaristic sandbox"; clips recorded in a "100 player Tactical All Out Warfare sandbox" | [1][4][5] |
| Is there an open-world sandbox map? | No official text says so. The mode is a King of the Hill style fight over a Control Zone "within larger maps" | [1][2] |
| How many maps? | Three maps with three variations each (Team17 press release, quoted via the foundation; not re-read here) | [9] |
| What is a "variation"? | Not defined in any official text read | [1][2][3] |

Assessment: Medium confidence that "sandbox" and "3 maps x 3 variations" are compatible. "Sandbox" describes freedom of play inside a map; the press release counts map assets. The official 18 Feb post describes "multiple locations and POIs" in the setting "Kolchia" [2], which could be what a "variation" refers to, but this is an inference and unconfirmed.

## Map scale: what official text says

| Value | As-of version | Source |
|-------|---------------|--------|
| Control Zone size: randomised 2x2 km | Steam page, Season 01 (checked 2026-10-08); also 18 Feb 2026 post | [1][2] |
| Map size: 256 km² | 18 Feb 2026 post (pre-release); not repeated on the Steam page | [2] |
| Max players per match: 100 | Season 01 | [1] |
| Teams: 3 | Season 01 | [1][2] |
| Points to win: 100 | Season 01 | [1][2] |

Assessment: Medium confidence that 256 km² remains current. It is official but dated seven months before launch, and the Steam page uses only "larger maps". The 2x2 km zone is 4 km², about 1.6% of 256 km² (arithmetic from [2]). Community figures (about 16 km edge to edge, 500 m radius play circles) are player-reported or unattributed, and the 500 m figure conflicts with the 2x2 km zone [12][13].

## Level design philosophy as stated

Official statements are thin. The 16 Jul 2026 devlog gives three points: real-world reference gathering in Georgia, continuous optimisation across a wide range of hardware, and tunable graphics options [3]. The 21 May 2026 Debrief lists "real-world ballistics, audio and flight models" and "100% player-driven militaristic sandbox" [5]. The Top Questions post says the setting offers "varied, grounded militaristic gameplay" with "multiple locations and POIs" [2]. No official text describes sightline, chokepoint or zone-placement design rules. Playtesters are quoted as surprised at performance, which is Bulkhead's own characterisation [3].

## What can be destroyed

| Item | Status | Source |
|------|--------|--------|
| Apartment blocks | Destroyable by rocket launchers | [1] |
| Towns and buildings generally | "Destructible battlefield"; tanks can "tear your way through towns" | [1] |
| Player buildables (FOB parts, schematics) | Destroyable; destruction reward scales with build progress since 0.1.2 | [7] |
| Terrain deformation | No official statement; a third-party roadmap claims terrain is destructible | [12] |
| Persistence across matches | No official statement | - |
| Which structures are indestructible | No official list | - |

Destruction is also a listed Early Access pillar: "Destruction & Build Mechanics" [2], and "Infantry, Vehicles, Base Building & Destruction" in the announcement trailer post [4]. The roles list includes Demolitions [4]. The gameplay trailer post lists "building, destruction" among the features [6]. Player-built structure rules are in fob-and-base-building.

## Destruction and performance

No official source ties destruction to a performance cost, a debris cap or a server tick budget. What is official: Bulkhead built a custom framework on UE5 to handle 100 players [2]; performance was prioritised from day one [3]; graphics options exist [3]. The Steam requirements and minimum spec are in system-requirements-and-performance. Assessment: Low confidence that destruction limits exist; the KB neither confirms nor denies them.

## Weather and rain (Season 02)

The official Season 02 teaser gives only the date, 15 Oct 2026 [8]. The 0.1.2 notes say Season 02 brings "new map conditions" [7]. Press reports that rain is an extra per-map weather state, not a dynamic mid-match event, quoting Bulkhead [10][11]. The Bulkhead text itself was not available in the saved official posts, so rain remains press-reported (confidence Medium). Whether rain affects visibility, vehicles or aircraft is unconfirmed [11].
