| Control Zone 2x2 km (4 km²), randomised | Season 01, checked 2026-10-08 | [1][2] |
| Map area 256 km² | 18 Feb 2026 official post | [2] |
| Max players 100; teams 3 | Season 01 | [1] |
| Points to win 100 | Season 01 | [1] |
| Maps 3, variations 3 each | Season 01 launch, press release | [9] |
| Minimum spec: GTX 1660 / RX 590, 16 GB RAM, 50 GB, 1080p Low 60 fps (upscaled) | Steam page, 2026-10-08 | [1] |
| Recommended spec: RTX 3070 / RX 6700 XT, 1440p Medium 70+ fps native or 4K Medium 60+ upscaled | Steam page, 2026-10-08 | [1] |
| Starting cash $10,000 | Season 01 | [1] |
| Buildable destruction reward scales with build progress | Patch 0.1.2, 30 Sep 2026 | [7] |
| Weather states at baseline: none documented; rain announced | Pre-Season-02 | [8][10] |
| Season 02 date 15 Oct 2026 | Teaser 22 Sep 2026 | [8] |

text:
Officially, WARDOGS launched with three maps, each with three variations [2], and a randomised 2x2 km Control Zone inside a 256 km2 map, set in a war-torn region called "Kolchia" [1][10]. Revised 2026-10-08 against the full text of all 32 saved Steam posts: none of them, nor the Steam store data, names Bakurani, Ozeti, Zestafona, Jutari or Saburtulo, profiles a map, or explains rotation [1][10][11][12]. The per-map profiles below therefore remain player-reported: Bakurani, Ozeti and Zestafona, plus the unconfirmed Jutari and Saburtulo [3][4][5][6][7].

Several community sources agree on the three names, their settings and the existence of roughly three rotating areas per map. They disagree on play-area size, control-zone counts and whether a fourth map exists. Rain is the only announced Season 02 environment change [8].

Confidence stays Low: the per-map names and profiles, which are the point of this document, are player-reported and the sources conflict. The official text only upgrades the generic map facts (256 km2 map, 2x2 km zone, "Kolchia"), which other documents already use.

text:
## Map profiles (all player-reported, Season 01)

| Attribute | Bakurani | Ozeti | Zestafona |
|-----------|----------|-------|-----------|
| Region label | Kavkazi [3] | Europe [3] | North America [3] |
| Setting | Eastern European mountain river valley [3][4][7] | Wooded river basin around a hill town [3][4][5] | Industrial rail hub on a river bend [4][5][7] |
| Relative size | Smallest [4] | About 4x Bakurani's play area [4] | About 4x Bakurani's play area [4] |
| Play-circle radius (community) | 500 m [3] | 550 m [3] | 500 m [3] |
| Terrain | Valley floor, factory district, forested ridges, farmland, snowy northern peaks [3][4] | Hill town, orchards, farmland, forest, river across the south [3][4] | Warehouses, rail yards, shipping, farmland, forest [3][4] |
| Named areas | Default, Farmland, Lumberyard [3][7] | Default, Church, River (Farmland defined but not in rotation) [3][7] | Default, Water Treatment, Houses (Small Factory defined but not in rotation) [3][6][7] |

## Notable points of interest (player-reported)

| Map | Features | Source |
|-----|----------|--------|
| Bakurani | Hill Town, Apartments, factory and containers, Water Silos, Bridge Hill, sunflower fields and church, Lumberyard, numbered towers (7 plus 4 abandoned in one list; 5 drill towers in another) | [4][7] |
| Ozeti | Walled football stadium with parking and garages, six-part Hillside Church, Apartments, Shops, Pool, Industrial, farms, 4 towers in two lists | [3][4][7] |
| Zestafona | Brick and numbered warehouses, factories, train sheds and tracks, Bus Depot, offices, water towers, northern Water Treatment, 3 drill towers | [4][6][7] |

## Typical Control Zone behaviour (player-reported)

- allthings.how: one objective ring of 85 m radius at the centre of the live play area; on Zestafona the three live areas are picked at equal frequency [3][6]. On Bakurani it says the Default area is picked twice as often as the other two [3]; no other source says this.
- allthings.how: the farthest area centres are 285 m apart on Bakurani, 693 m on Ozeti and 531 m on Zestafona [3][6]. These distances fit a 500 m circle model, not a 2x2 km zone.
- Hot Zone: roams inside the Control Zone and counts double [6][7]. Boostroom says Bulkhead confirms double cash for it; I could not trace that to an official page [7].
- Terrain effect: Bakurani high ground over the valley road decides engagements [3]; Ozeti open approaches to the town are exposed [3][7]; Zestafona has long exposed approaches in the yards [3][7].

## Unconfirmed maps

| Map | Claim | Source |
|-----|-------|--------|
| Bakurani Outskirts, Jutari | Sniper Showdown map on the Kavkazi world; 350 m play circle, 75 m objective ring, single fixed area, no rotation; status "not confirmed as playable" | [3] |
| Saburtulo | Listed as a King of the Hill map under Russia; no play area or objective; not playable | [3] |

No other source read mentions either name; the guides from xgamingserver.com, gamebrief.net and boostroom.com name only three maps [4][5][7]. Treat both as unconfirmed.

## Rotation

- Official: no rotation is documented. Bulkhead says only that the Control Zone is randomised [1].
- Player-reported: each map has three live areas drawn from a defined list of three or four; allthings.how says selection on Zestafona is equally likely [3][6]. Gamebrief says the whole map is not confirmed to reroll each match and no map vote or map order is documented [5].
- Assessment (Low): the "three variations" per map [2] plausibly match the three live areas, but no source states this.

## Conflicts between sources

| Topic | Source A | Source B | Treatment |
|-------|----------|----------|-----------|
| Play area | Official 2x2 km Control Zone [1][10] | 500 m radius circles, 85 m ring [3][6] | Not reconciled; official figure stands, community figures unverified |
| Whole-map size | Boostroom: 256 km2 attributed to Bulkhead [7] | Steam page gives no map size [1]; Bulkhead post of 18 Feb 2026 states 256 km2 [10] | Resolved: official, but pre-release; the Boostroom figure matches it |
| Control zones | 171 named zones across three maps [4] | One ring per map [3]; three to four positions per map [5] | No figure adopted |
| Map count | Three maps [2][4][5] | allthings.how introduction says four playable, details list three [3] | Three; internal inconsistency noted |
| Tower count | Bakurani 7 plus 4 abandoned [4] | Bakurani 5 drill towers [7] | Not reconciled |
| Bakurani rotation | Default picked twice as often [3] | No weighting documented [5][7] | Single source |

## Season 02 weather

Rain is reported by press as one extra weather state per map, set for the whole match; it does not change mid match, and the effect on visibility or gameplay was not stated [8]. The coverage mentions no new map [8]. Nothing else about the Season 02 environment is taken as fact here.

text:
Officially, WARDOGS is set in war-torn "Kolchia", where the fight is over a resource called PV-1, in "derelict industrial mountains of Eastern Europe" on a destructible battlefield [1][3]. Bulkhead's own 18 Feb 2026 FAQ states that three teams fight over "a randomized 2x2km Control Zone within a 256km² map" [3]. The map size is therefore official, though pre-release and not repeated on the Steam page, which says only "larger maps" [1]. The count of "3 maps x 3 variations" appears only in the Team17 press release, and "variation" is never defined [2].

The map names (Bakurani, Ozeti, Zestafona), their points of interest and relative sizes remain player-reported [14][15][16]. The official 0.1.2 post says only that Season 02 (15 Oct 2026) brings "new map conditions" [5]. Rain as a per-map weather state is press reporting of a Bulkhead post on X that is not in the saved official text [11][12]. No fourth map is announced.

Confidence is Medium (raised from Low in v1.0.0). Scale, setting, destruction headlines and the sandbox usage rest on official text; the named detail and the weather detail do not, and are labelled accordingly. Depth is in launch-maps-reference and destructibility-and-level-design.

text:
Verified 2026-10-08.

- Official: the setting is "derelict industrial mountains of Eastern Europe" with a destructible battlefield, in the fictional region Kolchia (Steam page, Season 01; FAQ 18 Feb 2026) [1][3].
- Official: the Control Zone is a randomised 2x2 km area within a 256 km² map (FAQ, 18 Feb 2026, pre-release). The Steam page repeats the 2x2 km zone and "larger maps" but not the total [1][3].
- Official: players can destroy apartment blocks with rocket launchers and tear through towns in armoured tanks; players can build and fortify key locations, for example a forward operating base at a chokepoint (Steam page, Season 01) [1].
- Official: Early Access includes "Destruction & Build Mechanics" (FAQ, 18 Feb 2026) [3].
- Press release (Team17, 10 Sep 2026): three maps, each with three variations [2]. No official Steam post in the snapshot repeats this count.
- Official: Season 02 is dated 15 Oct 2026 (22 Sep 2026 teaser, a video with a one-line text) and is described as "a larger content update, with new map conditions, equipment, balance reworks and additional features" (30 Sep 2026, patch 0.1.2 post) [5][7]. No rain statement appears in that official text.
- Press: rain is "an additional weather state per map and not a dynamic event mid match", attributed by Vice to a Bulkhead post on X that was not viewed [11][12].
- Official: patch 0.1.2 changed buildable-destruction rewards and buildable crit-spot behaviour; it has no map, terrain or weather entry [5]. The Season 1 changelog has one map-related fix (below) [6].
- Not verified: v1.0.0 cited the live Steam page for "large-scale maps with dynamic objective zones" and a plan for more maps and fighter jets; neither appears in the saved store JSON of 2026-10-08 [1]. Treated as unconfirmed.

text:
## Reconciling "sandbox" and "3 maps x 3 variations"

Official usage of "sandbox" is consistent across posts: "a large-scale, up to 100-player militaristic sandbox" with "building and destruction mechanics" on the Steam page, "100% player-driven militaristic sandbox" in the 21 May 2026 post, "makes the sandbox 100% player-driven" in the FAQ (about proximity chat), and a "100 player Tactical All Out Warfare sandbox" in the announcement trailer post [1][3][8][9]. It describes freedom of play, not a type of map. The map count comes only from the press release: three maps with three variations each [2]. The two are compatible.

"Variation" is undefined in every official text read [1][2][3][4]. A community guide lists about three named areas per map (for example Default, Farmland, Lumberyard on Bakurani) that come up from a rotation [16]. This plausibly matches "three variations" but is an inference, and the FAQ's "multiple locations and POIs" in Kolchia is an equally plausible referent [3]. Treat the equivalence as unverified.

## Player-reported map roster (Season 01)

Player-reported; see launch-maps-reference for the full profiles and the source conflicts.

| Map | Region label | Described terrain | Relative size | Source |
|-----|--------------|-------------------|---------------|--------|
| Bakurani | Kavkazi | River valley, town, factory district, snow-capped northern mountains | Smallest | [14][15][16] |
| Ozeti | Europe | Wooded river basin, hill town, walled football stadium, church, farmland | About 4x Bakurani | [14][15][16] |
| Zestafona | North America | River bend, warehouse and rail districts, shipping, farmland, forest | About 4x Bakurani | [14][15][16] |

A further "Bakurani Outskirts, Jutari" sniper map and "Saburtulo" appear in one roster but are listed as not confirmed playable [16]. They are not counted as launch maps. The "Georgia" in the devlog is a real-world reference-gathering trip, not a map name [4]. Assessment: the Georgian-sounding map names fit that trip, but no official text links them (confidence Low).

## Points of interest (player-reported)

| Map | Named features | Source |
|-----|----------------|--------|
| Bakurani | Hill Town, Apartments, Sunflower complex and church, Lumberyard, Water Silos, Bridge Hill, numbered towers | [15] |
| Ozeti | Stadium complex, hillside churches, Shops, Pool, Industrial, Lumberyard, farms, numbered towers | [15] |
| Zestafona | Brick and numbered warehouses, large factories, train sheds and tracks, Bus Depot, Offices, Water Towers, farmland | [15] |

One guide counts 171 control zones across the three maps [15]. Another records three or four zone positions per map and three live tower objectives on Zestafona [14]. These counts differ, so no figure is given as fact. The only official statement about locations is "multiple locations and POIs" [3].

## Size

| Claim | Value | Class | Source |
|-------|-------|-------|--------|
| Control Zone | Randomised 2x2 km | Official (Steam page and FAQ) | [1][3] |
| Whole map | 256 km² | Official (FAQ, 18 Feb 2026, pre-release) | [3] |
| Whole map, repeated | 256 km², fully destructible | Third-party roadmap | [13] |
| Whole world | About 16 km edge to edge | Player-reported | [16] |
| Play circle | 500 m radius (550 m Ozeti) | Player-reported | [16] |

Assessment: 16 km x 16 km equals 256 km², so the community figure is consistent with the official area if the map is square, which the official text does not say. Medium confidence that 256 km² still holds: it dates from seven months before launch and is absent from the Steam page. The 2x2 km zone is 4 km², about 1.6% of the map (arithmetic from [3]). The 500 m radius play-circle claim conflicts with the official 2x2 km zone and is not adopted [1][16].

## Destructibility

Official: a destructible battlefield where rocket launchers destroy apartment blocks and tanks tear through towns, and "the world around you reacts to your presence" [1]. "Destruction & Build Mechanics" is a listed Early Access pillar [3], and "Base Building & Destruction" is a trailer feature [9]. Since 0.1.2, rewards for destroying buildables scale with build progress [5]. No official source gives a per-structure destruction model, which terrain can be deformed, or whether damage persists across matches. A third-party piece says terrain as well as buildings can be reshaped [13]; official sources mention only buildings. See destructibility-and-level-design.

## Weather and time of day

The official Season 02 text says only "new map conditions" [5]; the teaser is a date and a video [7]. Rain as an additional per-map weather state, fixed for the match, is press reporting of a Bulkhead X post [11]. One press piece reports it is unconfirmed whether rain affects visibility or vehicles [12]. No day/night cycle is documented in any official text read. Whether "new map conditions" means rain, time of day or something else is unconfirmed.

This document does two jobs. First, it lists the channels BULKHEAD and Team17 are confirmed to use for WARDOGS, based on the official Steam posts saved locally on 2026-10-08. Second, it rates every outlet and site cited anywhere in this knowledge base for reliability, commercial conflict of interest and track record against the official text. It is the basis for future staleness and trust decisions.

The Steam store page and the Steam News hub are the only channels whose address and content are fully verified. On 2026-10-08 Steam showed 109,396 reviews (all languages), 74.3% positive, "Mostly Positive" [3].

text:
- **Official**: authored by BULKHEAD or Team17 (Steam announcements, official sites, press release). Source rank 1-3 in `SOURCE_REGISTRY.md`.
- **Press**: independent news outlet reporting on the game (rank 5).
- **Player-reported**: fan sites, guides, wikis, hosts, sellers (ranks 4 and 6). Never establishes a fact alone.
- **COI**: commercial conflict of interest, meaning the publisher sells something the article promotes (boosting, hosting, cash).
- **Reliability grade**: R1 matches official text and is usable as a secondary confirmation; R2 usable with corroboration; R3 lead only, label player-reported; R4 do not cite for facts. Grades are Assessment, not fact.
- **Baseline**: values recorded before the Season 02 wipe window so later diffs are mechanical.

Note the 1.25 million, 2 million and 3 million sales figures are the studio's own claims in its own posts; no independent audit is available.

## Source-class reliability scale

| Class | Typical sources | How the KB may use it |
|-------|-----------------|------------------------|
| Official (rank 1-3) | Steam page, Steam announcements, Team17 site and press release | Establishes facts, with date and version |
| Press, wire-style | Push Square, Pure Xbox, GamingOnLinux, Vice, MP1st | Confirms release and business facts; label as press |
| Press, aggregating | Gfinity, InGameNews, PlayDay, CoGConnected, GosuGamers, SteamDeckHQ | Cross-check only; re-verify against official text |
| Provider / seller | BisectHosting, XGamingServer, Boostroom, Supercraft, Timesaver | Player-reported with COI; never establishes a fact |
| Fan sites and guides | allthings.how, KeenGamer, Gamebrief, Neonsect, wardogs-game.com, wardogs.tech, Wardog Servers, wardogswiki.com, Dexerto wiki | Player-reported; use only where nothing official exists, labelled |
| Single-source or anonymous | MMOEXP, Gaming with Daopa, XGamingServer roadmap | Leads only |

## Outlet register

Grades: R1 reliable against official text, R2 usable with corroboration, R3 lead only, R4 do not cite alone. "Track record" is stated against the official Steam posts read for this document [2]. Where a row says "not tested", the outlet's claims in this KB have no official counterpart yet.

| Outlet / site | Class | COI | Track record against official text | Grade |
|---------------|-------|-----|-------------------------------------|-------|
| Steam store page and API | Official | None | Prices, date, developer, publisher and review counts are first-party [1][2][3] | Authority |
| Steam News (BULKHEAD posts) | Official | Self-reporting | Authority for patches, dates and studio claims. Studio sales figures are its own claims [2] | Authority |
| Team17 game page / support | Official | Publisher | Lists game and support; no contradiction found [4][5] | Authority |
| Team17 press release (gamedeveloper.com) | Official, republished | Publisher marketing | Dates and price claims agree with the Steam page; 21-23 Aug beta matches the official post [7][23] | R1 |
| Gfinity Esports | Press | None found | Season 1 changelog matches the official 9 Sep pre-load post on XP bands and prices, but labels it 10 Sep (the official post is dated 9 Sep) [12][24]. 0.1.2 notes match the official 30 Sep text [19][25]. Its 3-6 Sep beta dating is consistent with the official Closed Beta 02 and open-beta posts [10][11] | R1 |
| MP1st | Press | None found | 0.1.2 date (30 Sep) and 08:00 UTC window match [19][26] | R1 |
| Vice | Press | None found | 0.1.2 notes: 30 Sep, same window [19][27]. The Season 2 "rain" article cites a BULKHEAD statement that is not in the saved official posts [28] | R2 |
| InGameNews | Press | None found | Timestamps accurate: 0.1.2 at 06:57 UTC and the hotfix post at 00:13 UTC match the official posts to the minute [19][20][29]. Its ambiguity over whether the hotfix was scheduled is resolved by the official post: scheduled for 08:00 UTC, one hour [20] | R1 |
| PlayDay | Press | None found | 0.11 notes match the official 12 Sep post on browser split, persistent IDs and the 5% bonus [15][30] | R1 |
| Push Square, Pure Xbox | Press | None found | 1.25 million sold by 11 Sep matches the official post [14][31][32]; Xbox/PS5 2028 is not testable on Steam | R1 |
| GamingOnLinux, SteamDeckHQ | Press | None found | Linux/Proton statements come from developers; the studio's Steam feed itself carries GamingOnLinux items [2][33][34] | R2 |
| CoGConnected, GosuGamers | Press | None found | "Over 1 million" and "3 million in just over two weeks" agree with the official posts [14][18][35][36] | R1 |
| Gameluster | Press | None found | 1 million wishlists agrees with the official 14 Aug post [2][37] | R1 |
| PCGamesN, Rock Paper Shotgun, PlayGround.ru, SteamDB | Press / stats, seen in the feed only | None found | Bodies were not saved, so no track record could be tested; not cited as facts in this KB [2] | Not rated |
| KeenGamer | Press and guides | None found | Season 2 "confirmed features, rumors" mixes both labels in the title; progression guide is player-reported [38][39] | R3 |
| Dexerto wiki | Community wiki on a press brand | None found | Its Season 2 wiki asserts a wipe and Black Market that the official teaser does not state [17][40] | R3 |
| allthings.how | Guide site | None found | Maps/Control Zone figures conflict with the official 2x2 km Control Zone; "four playable battlegrounds" intro contradicts its own list [41][42] | R3 |
| Gamebrief | Guide site | None found | Maps/vehicle guides agree with the three-launch-maps count; no official counterpart for numbers [43] | R3 |
| Timesaver.gg | Seller blog | Yes (boosting/cash seller) | 2 Oct hotfix: IR rangefinder disabled and CIWS 12 s to 6 s agree with the official post [21][44]. Season 2 article: wipe, Gold Bar conversion and 16:00 UTC time are not in the teaser [17][45] | R3 for hotfix (verified), R4 for Season 2 |
| MMOEXP | Seller blog, single podcast | Yes (currency seller) | Dates the 0.1.2 patch to 29 Sep; the official post says 30 Sep [19][46]. Season 2 wipe claim not supported [17] | R4 |
| BisectHosting blog | Provider | Yes (approved host partner) | 0.1.2 admin notes (restart time, RCON) match the official text [19][22][47] | R2 |
| XGamingServer, Boostroom, Supercraft | Hosting / boosting sellers | Yes | Map guides and prices uncorroborated; hosting prices are pre-approval and not official [48][49][50] | R4 |
| wardogs-game.com, wardogs.tech, wardogservers.com, warcon (GitHub) | Unofficial fan and tool sites | Mixed (tracker/tool publishers) | Host count (two to three) is dated, not wrong, and the official 8 Sep post confirms three [22][51][52][53][54] | R3 |
| Neonsect | Fan guide | None found | Its three named hosts match the official 8 Sep post exactly [22][55] | R2 |
| wardogswiki.com | Unofficial wiki | Unknown | Season 2 page not corroborated by the teaser [17][56] | R3 |
| Gaming with Daopa | Community repost | Unknown | Closed-beta notes dated 14 Aug are not in the saved official feed; unverified [2][57] | R4 |

Assessment: ranking the outlets by agreement with official text, wire and aggregator press (Gfinity, MP1st, InGameNews, PlayDay, Push Square) is dependable on dates and patch contents; sellers and wikis are dependable only when an official post confirms the specific claim. Confidence High for the agreement findings (compared line by line to official text), Medium for the COI judgements (inferred from what each site sells).

## Where earlier KB documents are corrected or sharpened by official text

| Topic | Earlier KB wording | Official text | Effect |
|-------|--------------------|---------------|--------|
| IR Rangefinders and CIWS (2 Oct) | CWIS 12 s to 6 s "reported by a conflicted source"; battery rule "player-reported" | Official: Rangefinders disabled in the vendor until Season 02 where they "will require batteries"; CIWS now about 6 s versus 12 s [21] | Can be treated as official; supersedes the conflict note |
| Security hotfix (2 Oct) | Ambiguous whether scheduled or completed | Post at 00:13 UTC announces a planned 08:00 UTC fix on "Friday 2nd", one hour [20] | Resolved: scheduled |
| Closed beta dates | Open question whether 21-23 Aug and 3-6 Sep were one beta | Two betas: 21-23 Aug closed beta [7][8][9]; Closed Beta 02 announced 1 Sep, opened to all on 5 Sep until Sunday 08:00 UTC [10][11] | Resolved: two betas |
| Season 1 changelog date | 10 Sep | Official "Pre-Load Live & Season 1 Changelog" is dated 9 Sep [12] | Date should read 9 Sep for the notes, 10 Sep for launch |
| Season 02 wipe | Reported by Dexerto and Timesaver | Teaser contains only the date and a trailer; the 0.1.2 post says Season 02 has "new map conditions, equipment, balance reworks and additional features" [17][19] | Wipe remains unconfirmed |
| Hosting partners | Fan guide says QONZER, BisectHosting, xREALM | Official post names the same three on 8 Sep [22] | Confirmed |

All-language reviews on 2026-10-08 were 81,290 positive of 109,396 (74.3%), "Mostly Positive" [11].

Confidence is Medium. Prices, DLC contents, sales milestones, the monetisation policy and review counts rest on official Steam data. The console and Linux claims rest on press only and cap the document.

text:
## Editions (snapshot 2026-10-08)

The store snapshot (US and GB storefronts) shows the Standard and Supporter Edition options on the main page and the Supporter Pack as DLC; the pack's own entry also offers the Supporter Edition as the bundle [1][2]. The main page lists two DLC app ids (4809960 and 4809930); only 4809960 (Supporter Pack) was captured, so the second is unidentified [1]. Neither storefront showed a discount [1][2].

## Supporter Pack contents

The DLC entry says the pack "offers additional cosmetic content" and lists three "Starter Weapon" camos (Valkyra Branded A-91 Rifle, Lonestar Branded Bushmaster, Manticore Branded KH-2002), a Littlebird Helicopter "Taxi" camo, a Supporter Icon on the scoreboard (can be hidden in settings), a Grenade Bobblehead and a Helmet Bobblehead [2]. The identical list appeared in the 11 Aug 2026 announcement [4]. The developer's three stated rules: no monetisation during Early Access, in-game cash and gold bars are never monetised, and camos can never be directly purchased [2][4]. The launch press release repeats that cash, gold bars and status-based camouflage are not for sale [12]. Nothing in these sources lists a gameplay advantage, so cosmetic-only is the developer's statement, not independently tested.

## Platforms

The store snapshot flags Windows true, Mac false, Linux false; minimum OS Windows 10, recommended Windows 11 [1]. The official Steam posts in the snapshot contain no statement on Linux, Steam Deck, Xbox or PS5. A 3 Mar 2026 post lists "Console Release?" among questions answered, but the answer is in a video and not in the post text [10]. Press reports Xbox and PS5 versions for "sometime in 2028", and Xbox Store wishlists open on 10 Sep 2026 [13][14].

## Review snapshot

Steam's review summary (all languages, scope `language=all`) on 2026-10-08 was "Mostly Positive": 81,290 positive and 28,106 negative, 109,396 total, 74.3% positive [11]. The earlier English-only figure (79% of 63,179) is a different scope and is not comparable. Push Square recorded "over 17,000" reviews, also "Mostly Positive", on 11 Sep 2026 [14].

The US and GB rows come from the 2026-10-08 store snapshot; the other rows come from an earlier price-field fetch the same day and are not in the snapshot [3]. The Supporter Edition costs USD 10.00 / GBP 9.00 more than Standard, against USD 12.99 / GBP 11.99 for the pack alone, so the bundle saves USD 2.99 / GBP 2.99 versus buying both separately (arithmetic on the snapshot prices) [1][2]. Assessment: the Turkey price is far below the others; confidence High as a reading of the table, with no inference about intent.

## Early Access pricing and monetisation statements

The developer's 11 Aug 2026 post says its devlog covers "early access strategy, stair stepped pricing and long-term monetisation plans" but gives no price steps in the post text [4]. The press release describes a tiered model rewarding earlier backers and gives USD 39.99 [12]. No full-release price or Early Access end date appears in the snapshot posts or press release [4][12]. The 7 Apr 2026 post says a metagame (Black Market and Vault, Player Skills and Challenge System) will be built throughout Early Access; it states no pricing [8]. The 18 Feb 2026 FAQ states "No Battlepass. No Pay to Win. Earn cosmetics by playing." [9]. The developer also encourages refunds if the game or beta does not meet expectations [4].

## Pre-order and beta access

Pre-orders opened on 11 Aug 2026 for the 10 Sep Early Access launch and granted guaranteed access to the Closed Beta of 21 to 23 Aug; the developer said Steam key caps ended the old signup route [4].

## Platform roadmap and statements

| Platform | Status | Date of statement | Source and class |
|----------|--------|-------------------|------------------|
| Windows (Steam) | Live, Early Access since 10 Sep 2026; Windows flag true | 2026-10-08 | [1] official |
| Mac | Store flag false | 2026-10-08 | [1] official |
| Xbox | "Sometime in 2028"; wishlists open | 10 Sep 2026 | [13] press, not in official posts |
| PS5 | "Sometime in 2028" | 11 Sep 2026 | [14] press, not in official posts |
| Linux / SteamOS / Steam Deck | Store Linux flag false; Proton work ongoing per press | Aug to 25 Sep 2026 | [1] official flag; [15][16] press |

On 5 Sep 2026 the developers were reported to say "We do not officially support Linux and we cannot commit to having support for launch", that earlier Linux success in tests was by chance, and that buyers who expected Proton support could ask for a refund [15]. A developer comment dated 25 Sep 2026 (in the reader comments of that article) says there is no new timeline [15]. In August a developer was reported on the Steam forums as working on Proton support [16]. No Steam Deck Verified rating was found [16]. Reports about which anti-cheat blocks Linux are unconfirmed [15].

## Sales milestones (official Steam posts)

| Milestone | Date (UTC) | Source |
|-----------|-----------|--------|
| 1.25 million copies sold | 11 Sep 2026 | [5] |
| 2 million copies sold | 15 Sep 2026 | [6] |
| 3 million copies sold, "in just over 2 weeks since launching into Early Access" | 26 Sep 2026 | [7] |
| Peak 428,666 concurrent on Steam | about 13 Sep 2026 (press) | [17] |

Earlier drafts used press figures ("over 1 million" on 13 Sep and "3 million at 18 days"). The official posts supersede them: 3 million was announced 26 Sep, 16 days after the 10 Sep launch, not 18 [7][17]. The 1.25 million post carries no detail beyond the figure and an apology for delays [5]. The 2 million post's numbers snapshot is an image and was not read [6].

text:
WARDOGS is a 100-player, three-team tactical shooter developed by BULKHEAD (Derby, UK) and published by Team17 [1][2]. It entered Steam Early Access on 10 September 2026 at a Standard price of GBP 36.99 (UK) and USD 39.99 (US) [1][5]. A launch-day official post says consoles are coming in 2028 [18]. The launch was preceded by two closed betas: 21 to 23 Aug, then Closed Beta 02, announced 1 Sep and opened to everyone on 5 Sep [6][11][12].

Official Steam posts now confirm the full patch sequence: the Season 1 changelog (posted 9 Sep, at pre-load), Launch Stability Hotfix #1 (10 Sep), Patch 0.11 (announced 12 Sep, scheduled for 14 Sep), Update 0.1.2 (30 Sep), a security and stability hotfix (2 Oct) and an IR Rangefinder and CIWS balance hotfix (2 Oct) [17][19][21][25][26][27]. BULKHEAD announced 1.25 million copies sold on 11 Sep, 2 million on 15 Sep and 3 million on 26 Sep [20][22][24]. Season 02 is scheduled for 15 October 2026; the only official content text is "a larger content update, with new map conditions, equipment, balance reworks and additional features" [23][25]. Steam shows "Mostly Positive", 74.3% of 109,396 reviews in all languages [1].

Confidence is High. Dates, prices, patch contents, sales milestones and the Season 02 statement rest on official Steam posts and store data. Press is used only where no official text exists (console platform names, beta-participant figures) and is labelled. Season 02 content beyond the official text is unknown and is not asserted.

text:
## Developer, publisher and platforms

BULKHEAD is a Derby-based studio founded in 2015, previously known for The Turing Test and Battalion 1944; Team17 (part of everplay Group plc) publishes [2]. The Steam store data lists BULKHEAD as developer and Team17 as publisher, with Windows as the only platform (Mac and Linux false) [1][5]. Minimum OS is Windows 10 and recommended is Windows 11 [5]. Team17's game page also lists NVIDIA GeForce NOW [3]. The official launch-day post reads "COMING TO CONSOLES IN 2028" [18]; the PS5 and Xbox names and the "sometime in 2028" wording come from press (Sep 2026) [28][29]. Linux and Proton status is in editions-pricing-platforms.

## Editions and pricing (checked 2026-10-08)

| Item | GBP | USD | Source |
|------|-----|-----|--------|
| WARDOGS (Standard) | 36.99 | 39.99 | [1][5] |
| Supporter Edition (base game plus Supporter Pack) | 45.99 | 49.99 | [1][5] |
| Supporter Pack (DLC, sold separately) | 11.99 | 12.99 | [1][5] |

GBP 36.99 and USD 39.99 are the same Standard edition in two currencies; the Supporter Edition is a separate SKU [5]. The Supporter Pack is cosmetic only (camos, a scoreboard icon and bobbleheads). BULKHEAD's official pre-order post states there is no monetisation during Early Access beyond it, that in-game cash and gold bars will never be monetised, and that camos can never be bought directly [6]. Contents and regional prices are in editions-pricing-platforms. The pre-order post refers to "stair stepped pricing" [6], and the launch press release says the game is priced lower during Early Access with a higher price at full release; no full price is disclosed [2].

## Reception (checked 2026-10-08)

The saved Steam review summary shows "Mostly Positive" (score 6): 81,290 positive and 28,106 negative, 109,396 in total across all languages, about 74.3% positive [1]. Scope matters: version 1.0.0 of this document recorded 79% of 63,152 English-only reviews from the live page, a different filter, so the two figures are not a trend. Push Square recorded "over 17,000" reviews, also "Mostly Positive", on 11 Sep 2026, scope unstated [29].

## Developer roadmap statement

The official 7 Apr 2026 post says that throughout Early Access BULKHEAD is building a metagame including "The Black Market & Vault" and a "Player Skills & Challenge System"; the metagame foundation "is designed, but we will be building it throughout Early Access" [7]. The launch press release adds that work continues toward the wider meta game and long-term systems for 1.0 [2]. No dated roadmap to 1.0 is published; the only dated item is Season 02 on 15 Oct 2026 [23]. See season-2-announcements.

## Community channels

The Steam store page and Steam News hub for app 1867240 are the primary announcement channel [1][4]. Official posts confirm a community Discord ("10k+ members" on 9 Feb 2026), a community sign-up at community.wardogs.com, the Twitch show "The FPS Games Show" and three Approved Hosting Partners (QONZER, BisectHosting, xREALM) [8][9][13]. Team17's WARDOGS page links Team17's Discord, X and YouTube [3]. No WARDOGS Discord invite or X handle appears in the saved posts; see community-and-source-reliability.

The 3 to 6 Sep dates in the Gfinity changelog that v1.0.0 relied on match Closed Beta 02; the official posts are the authority for its window.

Concurrency figures differ by scope and date. The official 12 Sep post claims 400,000 peak concurrent users after launch [21]. CoGConnected reported 245,118 peak concurrent in the final playtest and nearly 500,000 Closed Beta participants (13 Sep) [30]. These measure different periods (launch weekend versus the pre-launch playtest), so they do not conflict. Push Square cited nearly 300,000 concurrent per SteamDB on 11 Sep [29]. Early Access content at launch was three maps with three variations each [2].

## Patch history

All rows rest on the official Steam posts. Full per-change lists are in patch-history.

| Date | Version | Headline changes | Source |
|------|---------|------------------|--------|
| 9 Sep 2026 (pre-load; live for launch) | Season 1 changelog | Church roof exploit fix, report tracking with weighted reports, server browser filtering rework, Z20 Lakota balance pass, crash fixes; XP curve slowed for levels 6 to 50 (level 20: 111,500 to 250,000); Artillery to Career 90, Heavy Tank to Driver 35; Forward Operating Base vendor price $2,500 to $7,500 and other price changes | [17] |
| 10 Sep 2026 | Launch Stability Hotfix #1 | Forced client restart and controlled login batches for join failures, unexpected kicks and long login queues | [19] |
| 12 Sep post; maintenance Mon 14 Sep 08:00 UTC | Patch 0.11 | Server browser split into Official and Community, text search and persistent Community Server IDs, more Asia capacity, cash exploit and GPU crash fixes, 5% end-of-match cash bonus on Community servers for one week; economy-abuse stance announced | [21] |
| 30 Sep 2026 | Update 0.1.2 (Minor Patch) | Fix for crash WD-L020 linked to Windows 11 update KB5124010; server-authoritative revive checks, vehicle fly-through reward cap, buildable and FOB pallet reward limits; new Deploy flow; admin daily restart, RCON AllowedHosts and message caps; zero-tolerance exploit warning | [25] |
| 2 Oct 2026 | Security and stability hotfix | Announced 2 Oct 00:13 UTC for 08:00 UTC the same day; "minor security and stability issues"; about one hour downtime | [26] |
| 2 Oct 2026 | IR Goggles and CIWS balance hotfix | IR Rangefinders disabled in the vendor until Season 02, where they will require batteries; CIWS destroys the Havoc in about 6 s instead of 12 s ("we overcorrected"); no client download or downtime | [27] |
| 15 Oct 2026 | Season 02 | Scheduled; see below | [23][25] |

The 0.11 post is an announcement dated 12 Sep with maintenance scheduled for 14 Sep; the saved posts include no separate deployed notice. The 2 Oct balance post is titled "IR Goggles" but its body names IR Rangefinders [27].

## Season 02 (scheduled)

BULKHEAD's "Season 02 Teaser" post of 22 Sep 2026 gives 15 Oct 2026 and a trailer; it states no launch time [23]. The 0.1.2 post calls Season 02 "a larger content update, with new map conditions, equipment, balance reworks and additional features" and promised more information "next week" [25]; the 26 Sep post made a similar promise [24]. No Season 02 detail post exists in the saved feed as of 2026-10-08, and the latest official post is the 2 Oct balance hotfix [27]. That hotfix also confirms IR Rangefinders return in Season 02 with batteries [27].

Official text contains no progression wipe, no cash-to-Gold-Bar conversion and no weather or rain statement. Those appear only in a boosting-seller article and a community wiki, and are player-reported and unverified [31][32]. Assessment: treat everything beyond the official lines as unconfirmed; confidence in the official lines is High, in any further Season 02 content Low. Graded rumours are in season-2-announcements, and the currency model is in season-reset-and-currencies.

- **Closed Beta weekend**: the 20 Aug post says the closed beta is "this weekend", that the NDA is lifted, that a first wave of invites went out and that 'WARDOGS Playtest' can be pre-loaded; the schedule itself is an image, so no dates are in the text [3]. The 24 Aug recap names pre-order access "between August 21st - 23rd" and says that weekend's closed beta is over [4]. 21-23 Aug 2026 is therefore the official closed beta window.
- **Closed Beta 02**: announced 1 Sep 2026 "ahead of The FPS Games Show" (3 Sep, 18:00 UTC) as a scale test, with access in waves for pre-orders, and tests named as server scaling and browsing, Twitch Drops, DLC entitlements, VOIP and the login queue [5]. The post gives no start or end date. A press-reported 3-6 Sep window is in the unconfirmed list.
- **Open beta**: on 5 Sep 2026 at 21:08 UTC the closed beta became an open beta "until the Beta ends - Sunday at 08:00 UTC" [6]. The Sunday after that post is 6 Sep 2026 (derived from the post date).

## 9 Sep 2026, Pre-Load Live & Season 1 Changelog (Official) [7]

The post is the Early Access launch changelog (launch 10 Sep 2026 [2]).

- Exploits: fixed an exploit reaching an unintended church roof position.
- Reporting and moderation: new report tracking system; reports weighted so repeat and bad-faith reporters carry less influence; cheater bans announced in server when match termination is off; the "kicked from server" message appears only if actually banned.
- Server browser and front end: reworked server browser filtering; community server images no longer scale incorrectly; Host a server button links to the hosting page.
- Voice chat: fixed voice cutting out permanently after a failed join (stale channel rejoins, push to talk targeting and re-login recover); improved reliability under load and added a visible communication status.
- Gameplay and vehicles: Z20 Lakota balance pass and sluggish pitch fix; helicopter input damping on every input device; maximum operator rotation speed for vehicle turrets; 155mm, 122mm and flare deployables take more loadout room; tank aiming DPI fix; Z20 Lakota chase camera rotation rattle reduced by 6 dB.
- Performance and stability: DLSS Frame Generation can be turned off without restart and the render target pool is configurable; fewer shadow cache refreshes; two frame generation crash paths fixed; more detailed GPU crash reports; a legacy graphics dependency removed; shadow quality clamped to Low on high benchmark scores; fixed crashes from off-thread network calls, closing a chatbox entry tooltip, buildables, and firing a weapon whose owner had left; dropped items no longer affect navigation; better startup reliability and messages.
- Progression: levels 10 to 20 slowed and the curve flattened from 35 onward; Artillery to Career level 90; Heavy Tank to Driver level 35; Forward Operating Base and Large Hammer vendor prices raised.

| Support | Large Hammer 7 to 8 |
| Driver | URAL 4 to 3; Kodiak Assault 8 to 6; Dune Buggy 10 to 8; Kodiak Flatbed 2 to 10; Large Supply Crate 20 to 16; URAL Covered 30 to 18; Music Tape H from Pilot 28 to Driver 23; URAL Attack 40 to 25; Humvee with minigun 35 to 30; Heavy Tank from Career 35 to Driver 35 |

## 10 Sep 2026, Launch Stability Hotfix #1 (Official) [8]

- A small client update. Logged-in players were forced to close and restart, then prompted to download the update; all players returned to the login queue and were admitted in controlled batches, gradually increased as players successfully populated servers.
- Targets: players unable to join servers, players kicked unexpectedly during play, extended login queue times.
- No gameplay or economy values changed in the post.

## 14 Sep 2026, Patch 0.11 (Official) [9]

Announced in the 12 Sep 22:26 UTC post. Maintenance on Monday 14 Sep 2026 at 08:00 UTC (01:00 US Pacific), about one hour.

- Server browser: front end split into Community and Official browsers; unnecessary filtering removed from Official (no official modified game modes); filtering reliability improved on Community; text search added to Community; Show Empty/Full added to the quick bar; Host button directed to the correct location.
- Community Server IDs persist between matches and restarts, and each server has a unique ID (longer for security); they were previously wiped on map change and restart.
- Server names: must sort alphabetically regardless of special characters and numbers; more than one space at a time is no longer allowed.
- Apology bonus: community servers give a 5% End of Match cash bonus for the next week.
- Other fixes: various cash exploits fixed; more GPU crashes addressed.
- Capacity: server capacity in Asia increased.
- Economy abuse sanctions: cash exploit or bug abuse gets a timed ban scaled to prior bans and a cash and XP reset to 0; content that tutorialises exploits without reporting is treated as advertising cheats (permanent ban); XP farming gets the most serious bans, with permanent bans for joining XP-farming servers for more than a few minutes.
- Listed as not yet ready: community server favouriting, tiered priority queues for Community servers, Message of the Day prompt, improved warmup activities, disabling AFK kicking during seeding, team switching controls.

## 30 Sep 2026, Update 0.1.2 (Minor Patch) (Official) [10]

Posted 06:57 UTC; maintenance at 08:00 UTC, estimated one hour.

- Crash fix: WD-L020 crash caused by Windows 11 update KB5124010.
- Cash and XP exploits: revive validity checks fully server authoritative; vehicle fly-through exploit fixed with capped rewards; buildable destruction rewards scale with build progress (destroying a placed schematic no longer gives a full reward); depositing pallets into a FOB outside the zone awards reduced rewards.
- Sanctions: players caught abusing cash and XP exploits or Real Money Trading had cash and progression reset and risk permanent bans; leniency for first-time offenders is over.
- Server browser and UI: new DEPLOY flow (Official, Community, Infantry Mode, Low-Level); Advanced Filters back on the Official list; long server names no longer truncated (hover for the full name); Join shows connecting then queue position; Anonymous mode hides the server name on the loading screen and in the pause menu unless shown; region select shows how many regions are selected; gamepad support on DEPLOY.
- Server admins: daily restart time (UTC); RCON AllowedHosts; RCON message and broadcast lengths capped; RCON defaults to Standard response detail rather than Full, and config responses no longer expose server internals; ServerImageURL checked when config loads.
- Server stability: various stability hotfixes and increased server security.
- Bugs: throwables (grenades, smoke, C4) blocked from enclosed vehicle seats; adaptive crosshair hides when aiming down sights; buildable crit spots no longer reappear in place, get pushed into corners or jump to the far side, and favour a reachable spot; Havoc bug causing extra damage from 20mm and 30mm cannon fire fixed; localisation improved.
- Forward look: Season 02 is described as a larger content update with new map conditions, equipment, balance reworks and features.

## 2 Oct 2026, two official posts

| Post | Time (UTC) | Contents |
|------|-----------|----------|
| WARDOGS / Security & Stability Hotfix [11] | 00:13 | Heads-up that a hotfix is planned "tomorrow, Friday 2nd" at 08:00 UTC for minor security and stability issues affecting some players; expected downtime one hour |
| IR Goggles & CIWS Balance Hotfix [12] | 15:39 | Two balance changes within 12 hours as regional servers restart; no new client download or server downtime |

- Security and stability hotfix [11]: the post gives no detail of the issues and does not mention gameplay, balance or economy. The date wording ("tomorrow, Friday 2nd") sits oddly with a post time of 2 Oct 00:13 UTC; the hotfix time is stated as 08:00 UTC on Friday 2 Oct, so the post was presumably written the evening before in an Americas time zone. Assessment: Medium confidence, inferred from the post time.
- Balance hotfix [12]: IR Rangefinders disabled in the vendor until Season 02, where they will require batteries; the CIWS now destroys the Havoc in around 6 seconds instead of 12. BULKHEAD says it overcorrected the CIWS in the previous patch and hotfixed it "this morning".
- Whether the 08:00 UTC security hotfix and the CIWS "this morning" hotfix are the same operation is not stated; the posts are treated as separate.

## Season 02 teaser (Official, not live) [13]

Posted 22 Sep 2026 at 16:53 UTC: "WARDOGS Season 02 is coming", dated 15 October 2026, "Stay tuned for more details". The 0.1.2 post adds that Season 02 is a larger content update with new map conditions, equipment, balance reworks and additional features [10]. Nothing else is official.

| "September 29" as the 0.1.2 date | One secondary article citing a podcast [17] | Contradicted by the official post (30 Sep) |
| Press name "Sea Whiz" for the Havoc anti-air change; claim that the 2 Oct security hotfix made no gameplay, balance, economy or UI changes | MMOEXP and InGameNews [17][15] | The official posts say CIWS and give no such statement for the security hotfix |

text:
This is a snapshot taken on 2026-10-08, one week before Season 02, of everything said about Season 02 and the longer Early Access roadmap. It exists so that after launch the real patch notes can be diffed against what was promised and what was rumoured. It deepens meta-release-foundation; it does not repeat its release timeline.

Officially, very little is confirmed. BULKHEAD's Steam post of 22 Sep 2026 gives only the date, 15 October 2026, and a video [1]. The 30 Sep 2026 Update 0.1.2 post describes Season 02 as "a larger content update, with new map conditions, equipment, balance reworks and additional features" [3], and the 2 Oct 2026 hotfix post says IR Rangefinders return in Season 02 and will need batteries [4]. Two promised "next week" detail posts had not appeared in the Steam News snapshot by 8 Oct 2026 [3][5].

Almost everything else (rain, a progression wipe, cash converting to Gold Bars, new weapons) is press or rumour. Confidence is Low: the core content claims are pre-release and come from press and from commercial sources that sell boosting or in-game cash. A table below grades each rumour so it can be scored after launch.

## Roadmap to 1.0

The roadmap post of 7 Apr 2026 states that the metagame is "our frontend experience that will enable you to continue earning, progressing and adding value to your account even when not in a match" [2]. The post lists two named systems, the Black Market & Vault and the Player Skills & Challenge System, with no season attached [2]. The post's text does not mention seasons, a wipe, or a conversion of cash to Gold Bars; third parties attribute those to the video embedded in it (see the rumour table) [2][15]. No official 1.0 date, Early Access duration or full-release price appears in the Steam posts in the snapshot. A podcast summary on a conflicted site quotes a developer as saying 1.0 is "roughly 23 months out" [17]; see Open Questions.

## Terminology conflict

Official text uses "GOLD MARKET" for the cosmetic store that Gold Bars buy from (18 Feb 2026) [8] and "The Black Market & Vault" for a planned metagame feature (7 Apr 2026) [2]. Dexerto says Gold Bars buy "exclusive cosmetics from the Black Market" [16]. Whether these are one store or two is not resolved by any official source.

text:
This depth document goes below the admin summary in technical-servers-foundation: the RCON HTTP API, the `ServerSettings.ini` keys, the 0.1.2 hardening, the 2 October hotfix, third-party admin tooling and moderation. It is verified against Season 1, patch 0.1.2 plus hotfixes to 2 Oct 2026.

Revision 1.1.0 re-checks the topic against the full official Steam posts. The official text says four things about RCON and server admin, all in the 0.1.2 post of 30 Sep 2026 under "Community Servers (for Server Admins)": a daily restart time in UTC, "RCON AllowedHosts: you can now set this to restrict who can access RCON", capped RCON message and broadcast lengths, and a Standard default response detail with config responses that no longer expose server internals [1]. It also says `ServerImageURL` "is now checked when the config loads" [1]. The official posts give no syntax, default or failure behaviour for any of these, and none of the other official posts read mentions RCON or AllowedHosts [2][3][4][5].

The 2 October security hotfix post says only that it addresses "minor security and stability issues affecting some players"; its text does not mention RCON [2]. Everything else (port, auth, endpoints, ini keys and defaults, the CL-501228 removals) still comes from an unofficial fan reference [8] and a tracker guide written by a tool vendor [9].

Confidence stays Low. The official text confirms the existence of the 0.1.2 admin changes but nothing about how the interface works, and the main reference was last updated before 0.1.2 shipped.

text:
- Official: Update 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026) lets server admins set "RCON AllowedHosts" to "restrict who can access RCON". The post gives no format, default or example [1].
- Official: 0.1.2 also caps RCON message and broadcast lengths (no values given) and makes Standard the default RCON response detail "instead of Full" [1].
- Official: the 2 Oct hotfix post links to "minor security and stability issues affecting some players" and does not mention RCON [2].
- Unofficial: the RCON interface is reported to be a versioned HTTP/JSON API (`/v1`), default port 7776, off by default, authenticated by a single shared bearer token with no read-only role (player-reported, reference v0.39 of 2026-09-21) [8][9].
- The fan reference does not mention AllowedHosts, because it predates 0.1.2; its key defaults may therefore be stale [8].
- Eight write endpoints were reported removed in build CL-501228 (14 Sep 2026) and replaced by edits to the config document. No official post says so; the official 0.11 post of the same date does not mention RCON [3][8].
- The listed `MaxPlayers` default of 128 is unexplained: the game is a 100-player format and no source gives a reason for 128 (see Detail and Open Questions) [8].
- Warcon and BattleMetrics are the named third-party panels; Warcon bans work only while the panel runs [9][10].

text:
State at Season 1 / 0.1.2 plus hotfixes, checked 2026-10-08.

- No official RCON or server-settings documentation was found. The vendor guide says so directly (guide dated 2026-09-14, PR) [9]. A fan site relaying a hosting-policy thread (checked 2026-09-01, PR) says Bulkhead was developing an RCON tool and that moderation details were unpublished at that time [11].
- Official, 0.1.2 post (30 Sep 2026, 06:57 UTC), section "Community Servers (for Server Admins)", quoted in full (O) [1]:
  - "Scheduled restarts: you can now set a daily restart time (UTC)."
  - "RCON AllowedHosts: you can now set this to restrict who can access RCON."
  - "RCON message and broadcast lengths are now capped."
  - "RCON now defaults to Standard response detail instead of Full, and config responses no longer expose server internals."
  - "ServerImageURL is now checked when the config loads."
- The same post lists, under "Server Stability Improvements", "Various server stability hotfixes" and "Increased server security to prevent exploitation", without saying whether these touch RCON [1]. Its summary says the update is aimed at thwarting XP and cash exploits "and security issues seen since the early access launch" [1].
- What the 0.1.2 post does not say: the AllowedHosts value format, wildcard support, default or failure behaviour; the cap values; what "Full" and "Standard" include; how to set the restart time [1].
- Also in 0.1.2: revive action validity checks are "now fully server authoritative" (an exploit fix, not RCON) [1].
- Security and Stability Hotfix: the Steam post is stamped 00:13 UTC on 2 Oct 2026 and announces a hotfix "planned for tomorrow, Friday 2nd, at 08:00 UTC, to address minor security and stability issues affecting some players", with "Expected downtime is one hour." Its text does not link the fix to RCON, AllowedHosts or server administration, and gives no other detail (O) [2]. A press outlet adds that it carried no gameplay, balance or UI changes (S) [6].
- Official moderation statements that apply to players rather than admins: the 0.11 post (12 Sep 2026) sets out penalties for economy abuse (timed bans with cash and XP reset, permanent bans for tutorialising exploits or XP farming) and says the studio tracks "every server you enter" [3]. The 0.1.2 post says leniency for first-time economy exploiters "is now over" [1]. The Season 1 changelog adds that cheater bans are announced in-server when match termination is turned off and that reports are weighted [5]. None of these describes admin-side ban tooling.
- The 8 Sep 2026 post says use the in-game report function on official servers and, for "the ultimate protection", play on community-hosted servers "where admins can instantly ban bad actors". It names three Approved Hosting Partners: QONZER, BisectHosting and xREALM [4]. It does not mention RCON.
- The 0.11 post (12 Sep 2026) is about the server browser: Community Server IDs persist between matches and restarts, server names are re-ordered and restricted. It does not mention RCON, AllowedHosts or build CL-501228 [3].

text:
## Transport and authentication (PR, reference v0.39, 2026-09-21) [8]

None of this table is stated in an official post.

| Item | Reported value |
|------|----------------|
| Base URL | `http://<host>:<port>/v1/` |
| Default port | 7776, settable in config or with `-RCONPort=` |
| Transport | Plain HTTP; HTTPS refuses the connection |
| Auth | `Authorization: Bearer <rcon-password>` on every request |
| Roles | One token, full read and write, no read-only key |
| Body format | JSON; the two config-document endpoints use `text/plain` |
| Errors | Non-2xx with `{error:{code,message}}`; 412 stale revision, 422 rejected value, 404 removed route |
| Rate limit | None published |

Conflict: the vendor guide says any listener bound beyond loopback "must use TLS" and that hosts provide an https address [9], while the fan reference says an earlier claim that a network listener needs a certificate was corrected and HTTPS is refused [8]. Both are player-reported and neither is confirmed by an official post. Assessment (confidence Low): terminate TLS in a reverse proxy or use a tunnel rather than expecting the game to do it.

## Endpoints (PR) [8]

| Group | Reported routes |
|-------|-----------------|
| Read | status, players, capabilities, bans, reserved-slots, audit (limit 1-500, default 50), config, rotation, catalog (maps, lightings, experiences, alternators), sponsor, server-id, health |
| Player writes | kick (reason), kill, message, faction change (only if listed in capabilities) |
| Match writes | broadcast, map change, match end, match restart, lighting |
| Bans | POST ban (steamId, optional reason), DELETE ban |
| Config | validate (dry run), PUT replace with `If-Match`, optional `force=true`, `fullApply=true` |

The vendor guide counts "around 35 endpoints" [9]. Clients should read `GET /v1/capabilities` rather than assume a route exists [8]. The official posts confirm that message and broadcast operations exist only indirectly, through "RCON message and broadcast lengths are now capped" [1].

## Config document semantics (PR) [8]

- `PUT /v1/config` replaces the whole document; omitted sections are removed.
- Every value is revalidated on each apply; one bad value blocks all edits, and a non-empty `errors` array means nothing was applied.
- Array keys follow Unreal operators: `!Key=ClearArray` empties, `.Key=value` appends.
- Ban, reserve and rotation commands edit and persist back to the ini. Only whitelisted sections and keys are honoured.

## ServerSettings.ini keys (PR; defaults as listed by the fan reference, not stated officially, not verified in-game) [8]

Only the existence of `ServerImageURL` as a config key with load-time checking is supported by an official post [1]. All other rows are player-reported.

| Section | Key | Listed default | Applies |
|---------|-----|----------------|---------|
| WDRCONSettings | `bEnabled` | listener off by default; the key list shows `true` (inconsistent) | startup |
| WDRCONSettings | `BindAddress` | 127.0.0.1 (0.0.0.0 = all interfaces) | startup |
| WDRCONSettings | `Port` | 7776 | startup |
| WDRCONSettings | `Password`, `PasswordHash` | empty password auto-generates to `Saved/RCON/ADMIN-PASSWORD.txt`; hash from `-GenerateRCONHash=` takes precedence | startup |
| WDGameSession | `ServerName` | none | immediately |
| WDGameSession | `ServerPassword` | empty (open) | next restart |
| WDGameSession | `ServerMin/MaxPlayerCash`, `ServerMin/MaxPlayerLevel` | 0 (no limit) | next restart |
| WDGameSession | `ServerImageURL` | none; 1024x256 PNG or JPEG on an allow-list | pending |
| WDGameSession | `MaxReservedSlots` | 20 | immediately |
| WDGameSession | `DefaultReservedPlayerIds`, `DefaultBannedPlayerIds` | one SteamID64 per line | n/a |
| Engine.GameSession | `MaxPlayers` | 128, clamped by a developer-set min and max | immediately |
| PreMatch PlayerCount | `MinimumRequiredPlayers` | 60 | next match |
| KOTH | `ScorePeriod` | 24 s, range 18-30 | next match |
| WDGameStateSession | `bLockOverpopulatedTeamsConfig`, `OverpopulatedTeamThresholdConfig` | true, 2 | next match |
| MapRotationSettings | `bEnabled`, `RotationMode`, `+RotationEntries` | true, Ordered (or Random) | immediately |

The reference states the RCON listener is off by default yet lists `bEnabled` as `true`; this inconsistency is unresolved, so treat the true default as unknown [8]. No `AllowedHosts` key name, section or default appears in any source: the official post names the setting only as "RCON AllowedHosts" in prose [1].

## MaxPlayers 128 versus a 100-player game

- The game format is 100 players in three teams (Steam page, via the foundation document). No official post read gives a server `MaxPlayers` value, and a web search of hosting wikis found no source for 128; those pages were not opened and are not relied on.
- The reference says the value is "clamped by a developer-set min and max" [8]. So 128 is at most a stored default, and the effective cap could be lower.
- Assessment (confidence Low): 128 is probably an engine-level or template default, not a supported player count. This is inference. Do not set it above 100 expecting more players, and confirm the clamp with your host.

## Build CL-501228 removals (PR, build dated 2026-09-14) [8]

Removed routes (now 404 on current builds, still served by older builds): `PATCH /v1/settings`, `POST` and `DELETE /v1/reserved-slots`, `POST` and `DELETE /v1/rotation/entries`, `POST /v1/rotation/entries/{i}/move`, `POST /v1/rotation/save`, `PUT /v1/sponsor`. The functions moved to config keys: `DefaultReservedPlayerIds`, `RotationEntries` with `bEnabled` and `RotationMode`, `ScorePeriod`, `ServerImageURL`. The build date coincides with the maintenance window of patch 0.11 (announced for 14 Sep 2026) [3], but the 0.11 post does not mention RCON or these removals, so no source ties the two explicitly.

## Hardening in 0.1.2 and the hotfix

| Change | Class | Note |
|--------|-------|------|
| "RCON AllowedHosts: you can now set this to restrict who can access RCON" | O [1] | Value format, wildcard and default are not stated in any source read |
| RCON message and broadcast lengths capped | O [1] | Cap values not published |
| Standard response detail by default "instead of Full" | O [1] | Whether Full is still selectable is not documented |
| Config responses no longer expose server internals | O [1] | Which fields were hidden is not documented |
| `ServerImageURL` checked when the config loads | O [1] | Consistent with the reference's allow-list note [8], which is not official |
| Scheduled daily restart time (UTC) | O [1] | How to set it is not documented |
| "Increased server security to prevent exploitation" | O [1] | Does not say RCON |
| Server-authoritative revive checks | O [1] | Gameplay exploit fix, not RCON |
| 2 Oct hotfix: "minor security and stability issues affecting some players" | O [2] | Text does not link to RCON; contents undisclosed |

## Admin tooling and moderation

- **Warcon** (PR, repository page): self-hosted panel (Bun, SvelteKit, Postgres, Docker Compose), MIT code, with map imagery excluded from the licence and owned by Bulkhead. Per-server roles viewer, operator and admin; stored RCON passwords encrypted (AES-GCM); audit log exportable to CSV or JSON; automation triggers. No game version is stated and commit dates were not visible [10]. The page says the protocol was reverse-engineered, so it can break when builds change [10].
- **Warcon bans** are enforced by the panel's worker, not the game: a banned player is removed when seen, and bans only hold while Warcon runs and reaches the server. Bans made outside the panel appear as "local" [10].
- **BattleMetrics** is reported to support WARDOGS RCON, paid after a free tier, and it stores your RCON password [9]. The vendor guide is by Warcon's publisher, so it is promotional [9].
- **Native bans:** by Steam ID, persisted in the ban list and `DefaultBannedPlayerIds` [8][9]. Officially, only the 8 Sep statement that community admins "can instantly ban bad actors" supports the existence of admin-side bans [4].

text:
This depth document extends the technical-servers-foundation with how WARDOGS servers are obtained and found: the hosts-only model, the approved hosts, the Official and Community split introduced in patch 0.11, regions, browser behaviour, slot counts, restart handling and prices. Version 1.1.0 is revised against the full official Steam posts (snapshot of 8 Oct 2026), which were unreadable when version 1.0.0 was written from fan relays. It is verified against Season 1, patch 0.1.2 and hotfixes to 2 October 2026. Season 02 is reported for 15 October 2026 and is outside this version.

Headline findings: the studio's own 8 September 2026 post names three Approved Hosting Partners, QONZER, BisectHosting and xREALM, and says Community Hosted Servers could be pre-ordered through them ahead of the 10 September launch [1]. That settles the two-versus-three conflict: the two-host figure was a fan-site statement dated 1 September [9]. The patch 0.11 browser changes and the 0.1.2 Deploy flow, restored Official filters and daily restart time are now confirmed from the official posts [2][3]. What remains unofficial is the self-hosting and server-code position, prices, slot tiers, regions and any default restart interval. The 12-hour versus 24-hour restart conflict is still unresolved: the official post states only that admins can set a daily restart time in UTC [3].

Confidence is Medium. The hosting model, host names, browser split and restart mechanism rest on official posts; prices, slot sizes, regions and the server-code claim rest on fan sites and commercial pages and are labelled player-reported throughout.

- Official (patch 0.11, 14 Sep 2026): the browser split into Community and Official; Official lost its filters because there are no Official modified game modes; Community gained text search and filter reliability fixes; Show Empty/Full was added to the quick bar [2].
- Official: Community Server IDs persist across matches and restarts, are unique, and are longer for security [2].

text:
Statements at Season 1 / patch 0.1.2, checked 2026-10-08.

- **Approved hosts.** Three Approved Hosting Partners: QONZER, BisectHosting and xREALM (official, 8 Sep 2026) [1]. A tracker (updated 14 Sep 2026) also says three exist and agrees [11].
- **Hosting model.** Community servers are bought through those partners [1]. That self-hosting is unavailable and that the developer withholds server code is player-reported only (fan site, evidence dated 1 Sep 2026) [9]; a second guide says no other host has access to the server code [10].
- **Browser.** Community and Official lists since 14 Sep 2026 [2]. The 0.1.2 Deploy flow offers Official, Community, Infantry Mode and Low-Level, and advanced filters are back on the Official list [3].
- **Restart.** Admins can set a daily restart time in UTC (official, 0.1.2) [3]; BisectHosting repeats this [7].

text:
## Resolving the host count (2 versus 3)

| Date of evidence | Claim | Source | Class |
|------------------|-------|--------|-------|
| 1 Sep 2026 | Two hosts passed launch standards, names unpublished, more in the pipeline | [9] | Fan site |
| 7 Sep 2026 | Studio names QONZER and BisectHosting (relayed) | [10] | Fan guide, unconfirmed |
| 8 Sep 2026 | Three Approved Hosting Partners named: QONZER, BisectHosting, xREALM | [1] | Official |
| 14 Sep 2026 | "Only the three approved hosts run WARDOGS servers" | [11] | Tracker |

Assessment: confirmed. The conflict was stale evidence, not disagreement, and the official post names the same three the fan guide listed. Confidence High on the three names, resting on [1]. The fan guide's claim that the first two were named on 7 Sep and xREALM added on 8 Sep is not supported by the official post, which names all three together; no 7 Sep post is in the snapshot, so the stepwise dating stays unconfirmed [10]. Other sellers (XGamingServer, Survival Servers, LOW.MS, Supercraft) advertise WARDOGS hosting but are not on the official list; XGamingServer itself says it is "onboarding" through partners and does not claim approval [13][14]. Treat such pages as pre-approval marketing.

## Official versus Community (patch 0.11, 14 Sep 2026) [2]

| Aspect | Official | Community |
|--------|----------|-----------|
| Operator | Bulkhead | Approved host customer |
| Filters | Removed in 0.11 (no Official modified modes); advanced filters added back in 0.1.2 [3] | Reliability improved, text search added |
| Quick bar | Show Empty/Full added to the browser quick bar (post does not split by list) | Same |
| Server ID | Not stated | Persistent, longer, unique, joinable by ID |
| Naming | Names sorted alphabetically regardless of special characters and numbers; no repeated spaces | Same |

The post frames the change as favouring community servers: it admits Community Servers "have been underserved" and that the studio rushed its Community Server strategy [2]. The studio notes that matchmaking would suit a game of this size but that it does not want community admins and hosts to suffer, hence the two browsers [2]. The Host button was updated to direct to the correct location [2]. PlayDay's press summary matches the official text [8].

Planned and not shipped per the 0.11 post: community server favouriting, tiered priority queues for Community servers, Message of the Day prompt, improved warmup activities, disabling AFK kicking during seeding, and team switching controls [2]. A one-week 5 percent End of Match cash bonus on Community servers ran from 14 Sep and has ended [2].

## Browser behaviour

- Official: 0.1.2 shows your place in the queue after clicking Join, no longer truncates long server names (hover shows the full name), and adds gamepad support on the Deploy screen [3].
- Region is picked via Deploy, Server Browser, Region, tick regions, Confirm (player-reported guide) [12]. The official 0.1.2 note says only that region select now shows how many regions are selected [3].
- Ticking several regions has been reported to return an empty list; guides advise selecting one and clearing persisted search text (player-reported) [10][12]. A fan site calls the one-region rule a temporary August Beta workaround, not a confirmed Early Access rule [9].
- Official: Asian capacity was increased in 0.11; no slot or per-region figures were published [2].

## Regions

| Source | Regions named | Class |
|--------|---------------|-------|
| Official 12 Sep post | "The Asian region" capacity increase only; no list | Primary [2] |
| Tracker, 14 Sep 2026 | Europe, North America East, North America Central, North America West, Oceania, Asia, South America | Player-reported [11] |
| Guide screenshot caption | Europe, North America, South America, Asia, with ping values | Player-reported [12] |
| Hosting vendor | Datacentres in East/West USA, Europe (Germany), Oceania, Singapore | Commercial [13] |

No official region list was found; labels disagree. Oceania as a browser region is unconfirmed [9][12]. The time-zone table in the 12 Sep post is a maintenance schedule, not a region list [2].

## Slots and capacity

No official post read states slot counts for community servers. Matches are 100 players across three teams per the foundation. Hosts sell by different units: xREALM 60, 80 or 100 player packages; QONZER sells by CPU threads (8, 10 or 12) and says it does not limit slots; the smallest size sold anywhere is 60 slots (player-reported compilation, 13 Sep 2026) [10]. The unofficial config reference lists `MaxPlayers` default 128, "clamped by a developer-set min/max" [15].

## Costs (provider pages as compiled 13 Sep 2026; verify before buying; no official price) [10]

| Host | Price shown | Notes |
|------|-------------|-------|
| QONZER | GBP 49.95, 59.95, 69.95 per month | 5% quarterly, 10% semi-annual, 15% annual prepay discounts |
| BisectHosting | from USD 71.99 per month | per-tier prices not visible |
| xREALM | from EUR 59.99 per month | 60/80/100 slots |

Roundups conflict with these figures [10]. Pre-approval pages quote far lower numbers (for example XGamingServer USD 24.50 to 42.00 and a Supercraft reservation page USD 17.99 to 39.99), marked "coming soon" or reservation-only [13][14]; they are not approved-host prices.

## Restart cycles (12 h versus 24 h)

- Official: "Scheduled restarts: you can now set a daily restart time (UTC)" for community server admins, in 0.1.2 [3]. This is a once-per-day schedule, which fits "24 h", but the post states no default or minimum interval.
- Not documented: the unofficial config reference lists no scheduled-restart key, only on-demand `POST /v1/match/restart`; some session keys apply only at next restart [15].
- The 12 h figure was not found in any official post or any source I could open. The foundation's statement that host guides disagree remains unverified. Persistent IDs mean a restart no longer changes a server's identity [2].
- Whole-service maintenance is a separate matter: official one-hour windows at 08:00 UTC on 14 Sep, 30 Sep and 2 Oct [2][3][4].

## How a prospective admin gets a server

1. Choose one of the three Approved Hosting Partners (QONZER, BisectHosting, xREALM) [1]. 2. The in-game Host button links to the hosting page [2][6]. 3. Check slots, region, billing term and refund terms on the host's own page (player-reported advice) [9]. 4. RCON was described in August as in development, with day-one controls limited to maps and modes [9]; RCON additions including AllowedHosts arrived in 0.1.2 [3] (see rcon-and-server-admin).

This depth document goes beyond the specification table in technical-servers-foundation. It collects what is officially documented about client performance and stability in WARDOGS (Steam app 1867240): the Steam store requirements as returned by the store API in the US and GB storefronts, what the official posts say about upscaling and frame generation, the Linux and Proton position, the WD-L020 crash and its Windows 11 KB5124010 link, and a post-by-post list of performance and crash fixes through the 2 October 2026 hotfixes [1][2][3][4][5][6][7].

Headline facts: the store lists a 50 GB install, 16 GB RAM and a 1080p Low 60 fps (upscaled) minimum, lists Windows only, and carries no DirectX, VRAM or storage-type line [1]. Update 0.1.2 (30 September 2026) officially names a "Windows 11 'WD-L020' Crash Error Fix" and attributes the crashes to Windows 11 update KB5124010 [5]. The only official upscaling or frame generation wording is a DLSS Frame Generation toggle fix in the Season 1 changelog [2]. The developers' own posts say nothing about Linux, Proton, Steam Deck or the name of the anti-cheat [1][10].

Confidence is Medium overall. The specification table is a direct reading of the store snapshot and is rated High; the Linux position rests on one press article and the settings guidance is player-reported.
