## Specification wording (Steam store API, US and GB, snapshot 2026-10-08) [1]

Confidence: High. The US and GB storefront payloads are identical.

| Item | Minimum | Recommended |
|------|---------|-------------|
| Architecture | 64-bit processor and operating system | 64-bit processor and operating system |
| OS | Windows 10 | Windows 11 |
| CPU | Intel Core i5 8600, AMD Ryzen 5 3500 | Intel Core i7 12700k, AMD Ryzen 7 5700x |
| RAM | 16 GB | 16 GB |
| GPU | Nvidia GTX 1660, Radeon RX 590 | Nvidia RTX 3070, AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT |
| Storage | 50 GB available space | 50 GB available space |
| Network | Broadband Internet connection | Broadband Internet connection |
| Additional notes | 1080p Low @ 60fps (Upscaled) | 1440p Medium @ 70fps+ (Native) or 4k Medium @ 60fps+ (Upscaled) |
| DirectX | Not listed | Not listed |

Gaps in the official figures: no VRAM, no storage type (SSD or HDD), and no DirectX or Vulkan statement [1]. The minimum tier pairs a GTX 1660 class GPU with an "Upscaled" target, so players near the minimum should expect to rely on an upscaler. Assessment: that reading is an inference from the note wording, Confidence Medium, resting on [1].

Other store data: supported languages are English (full audio), French, Italian, German, Spanish - Spain, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Polish, Turkish and Ukrainian; accessibility tags include Camera Comfort and Custom Volume Controls [1].

## Graphics and upscaling settings

- **Documented officially:** the Season 1 changelog says DLSS Frame Generation can be turned off without restarting and the render target pool is configurable; shadow quality is clamped to Low on high benchmark scores rather than being switched off entirely; shadow cache refreshes were reduced, which cuts hitching when taking control of a character; dropped items no longer affect navigation, "which claws back a little performance"; a legacy graphics dependency was removed [2].
- **Official intent:** a 16 Jul 2026 devlog post states that performance "has been a priority for the entire team since day one", that the game was optimised "across a wide range of hardware" and that graphics options let players tune it to their PC; it gives no figures [8].
- **Not documented in the sources read:** an FSR or XeSS option list, DLSS quality modes, or a Reflex entry. No official post mentions FSR, XeSS, Reflex or VRAM [2][5].
- **Player-reported settings guide** (allthings.how, "Updated Sep 12, 2026"): lists an Overall Quality Custom profile; Global Illumination as the biggest single gain at roughly 20 percent on average; Shadows, Reflections, Shading, Post-Processing and Particle Spawn Rate at Low; Texture Streaming reduced first on VRAM warnings; DLSS on RTX cards and FSR on others, with Quality as the usual balance; Nvidia Reflex and a frame limit matching refresh rate [12]. These are one site's recommendations, not developer guidance, and the figure is not independently measured. Treat all settings advice as player-reported.

## Linux, Steam Deck and Proton

| Date | Statement | Source |
|------|-----------|--------|
| 2026-10-08 | Store API: platforms Windows true, Mac false, Linux false; Linux requirements empty | [1] |
| 5 Sep 2026 | Developers "cannot commit to having Linux support for our Early Access launch"; still working on Proton compatibility (press report) | [11] |
| 5 Sep 2026 | An earlier community-manager Discord post implying support was called a communication mistake; earlier Linux functionality in tests was accidental (press report) | [11] |
| 5 Sep 2026 | Buyers who expected Proton support on 10 Sep were told to refund (press report) | [11] |

The Steam news posts in the snapshot (official posts, February to 2 October 2026) contain no mention of Linux, Proton or Steam Deck, so the developers' position rests on the GamingOnLinux report. No Deck Verified rating was found; treat Deck as unsupported and untested.

## Anti-cheat disclosure

- Fact: the live Steam page was read earlier as stating the game "Uses Kernel Level Anti-Cheat". That wording does not appear in the store API snapshot, which carries no anti-cheat field, so it is not re-confirmed from the snapshot [1].
- No official source names the product. The developers' 8 Sep 2026 post says "There's a rule in game development: you don't talk about anti-cheat" and points players to the in-game report function and community-hosted servers [10]. GamingOnLinux says the game previously used Easy Anti-Cheat and the developers appeared to be testing something else; this document does not name the product [11].
- Moderation side: the Season 1 changelog added a report tracking system, weighted reports, and in-server announcements of cheater bans [2]; see technical-servers-foundation.
- Assessment: a kernel driver generally installs at game launch, needs administrator rights, and commonly conflicts with Linux compatibility layers unless the vendor enables Proton support. Confidence Low to Medium: this is general reasoning, not a WARDOGS-specific statement.

## WD-L020 and KB5124010

- The 0.1.2 post (30 Sep 2026) lists "Windows 11 'WD-L020' Crash Error Fix" as a key update, and states: "Fixed the issue caused by the latest Windows 11 update, KB5124010, causing the recent WD-L020 crashes." [5]
- It was part of a minor patch aimed mainly at XP and cash exploits and security issues, with about one hour of maintenance from 08:00 UTC [5].
- No official post describes the mechanism, which hardware was affected, or a pre-patch workaround. No source recommends uninstalling the Windows update; do not infer it.

## Performance and settings changes at launch (Season 1 changelog, 9 Sep 2026) [4]

- DLSS Frame Generation can be turned off without a restart; the render target pool is configurable.
- Shadow cache refreshes were reduced (less hitching when taking control of a character); shadow quality is clamped to Low on high benchmark scores rather than switched off.
- Dropped items no longer affect navigation.
- Startup reliability improved with clearer early-failure messages and a recovery route; a legacy graphics dependency was removed.
- Crash fixes covered two frame generation paths, network calls scheduled off the game thread, a chatbox tooltip, buildables, and firing a weapon whose owner had left. GPU crash reports carry more detail.
- Voice chat recovery after a failed join and under load was improved, with a visible communication status.
- Launch day: a client hotfix on 10 Sep forced a restart and staged re-entry through the login queue to address players unable to join, unexpected kicks and long queues [5].
- Netcode: none of the official text read describes tick rate, prediction or lag compensation. This is a gap, not a finding.

## Moderation and anti-cheat systems

- Report tracking: reports are weighted so repeat and bad-faith reporters carry less influence; cheater bans are announced in server when match termination is off; the "kicked from server" message appears only for real bans [4].
- Economy abuse (patch 0.11 post): cash exploits get a timed ban plus a reset of cash and XP to 0; content that tutorialises exploits is treated as advertising cheats and risks a permanent ban; the developer states "We track every server you enter" and joining known XP farming servers for more than a few minutes risks a permanent ban [6].
- 0.1.2 (30 Sep): leniency for first-time offenders is declared over; players caught abusing repeatable exploits or Real Money Trading risk permanent bans without warning [7].

## Server browser timeline

| Date | Change |
|------|--------|
| 10 Sep 2026 (Season 1 changelog, 9 Sep) | Filtering reworked; Host a server button links to the hosting page; community image scaling fixed [4] |
| 14 Sep 2026 (0.11) | Community and Official browsers; filters removed from Official; text search and Show Empty/Full on the quick bar for Community; persistent, longer unique server IDs; server names ordered alphabetically with single spaces only; Asian capacity increased; 5% End of Match cash bonus on Community servers for one week [6] |
| 30 Sep 2026 (0.1.2) | Deploy flow (Official, Community, Infantry Mode, Low-Level); Advanced Filters restored to Official; long names no longer truncated; queue position shown after Join; gamepad support on the Deploy screen [7] |

Planned but not shipped per the 0.11 post and not announced as shipped in 0.1.2: community server favouriting, tiered priority queues, Message of the Day prompt, improved warmup activities, disabling AFK kicking during seeding, team switching controls [6][7].

text:
Source warning: Bulkhead has published no server-admin manual that was found. Only the 0.1.2 admin changes below are official; the RCON and config reference is unofficial, predates 0.1.2 and is labelled Low confidence.

**Hosting model.**

- Official: community hosted servers are sold through three Approved Hosting Partners, QONZER, BisectHosting and xREALM, per the 8 Sep 2026 post [3]. The in-game Host button links to the hosting page [4][6].
- The 2-versus-3 conflict is resolved by dating: a fan site relaying evidence checked on 1 Sep 2026 said two unnamed hosts had passed launch standards [13]; a tracker updated 14 Sep 2026 says three [15]; the official post of 8 Sep confirms three and names them [3].
- Player-reported only: the fan site says server code will not be released for everyone to host (citing performance and security) and the tracker says RCON access depends on the host's panel [13][15]. No official statement of a hosts-only model, or of the absence of a downloadable dedicated server, was read in the snapshot. Consequence for admins: you probably cannot run your own SteamCMD or Docker server; confirm with your host. Detail in server-hosting-and-browser.

**Admin changes confirmed in 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026, official)** [7]:

- Scheduled restarts: a daily restart time can be set (UTC).
- RCON AllowedHosts setting to restrict who can access RCON.
- RCON message and broadcast lengths are capped.
- RCON now defaults to Standard response detail instead of Full, and config responses no longer expose server internals.
- ServerImageURL is checked when the config loads.
- Since 0.11, community server IDs persist across map changes and restarts and are longer for security reasons [6].

**Unofficial RCON and config reference** (wardogs.tech, self-described as not official docs, version 0.39, written before 0.1.2; player-reported, Low confidence) [14]:

- RCON is plain HTTP REST with JSON, base `http://<host>:<port>/v1/`, default port 7776 (`-RCONPort=`), no TLS, so the password crosses the network in clear text.
- Authentication is `Authorization: Bearer <rcon-password>`; one token has full read and write access with no read-only role. The listener is off by default (`bEnabled` in `[/Script/WDRCON.WDRCONSettings]`).
- Endpoint groups: status, players, bans, config, rotation, capabilities; writes include kick, kill, message, ban, broadcast and match map/end/restart. `PUT /v1/config` replaces the whole document and supports `If-Match` revision checks.
- Listed `ServerSettings.ini` keys include `ServerName`, `ServerPassword`, `ServerImageURL` (1024x256), cash and level min/max limits, `MaxReservedSlots` (default 20), `MaxPlayers` (listed default 128), `MinimumRequiredPlayers` (default 60), KOTH `ScorePeriod` (default 24 s) and map rotation (`Ordered` or `Random`).
- Several endpoints were reported removed in build ++Wardogs+Live-CL-501228 (2026-09-14) in favour of the config document [14]. Because the reference predates 0.1.2, response detail defaults and config output may now differ (the official 0.1.2 notes say Standard detail is now the default and config no longer exposes internals) [7].
- Assessment: because RCON as documented uses one shared secret over unencrypted HTTP, the official AllowedHosts setting [7] should be used and RCON kept on a private network or behind a TLS proxy. Confidence Low to Medium: the AllowedHosts fact is official, the transport detail is unofficial [14].

**Third-party tools** (player-reported, not endorsed): Warcon, an open-source (MIT) self-hostable multi-server RCON panel with per-admin roles and audit log [16]; BattleMetrics has reportedly added WARDOGS RCON support [15]. The guide at [15] was written by Warcon's builders, so its recommendations are promotional. See rcon-and-server-admin.

**Restart timers.** Host guides disagreed on any built-in restart timer (12 h versus 24 h of uptime); this is unverified. The only official restart statement is the configurable daily UTC restart time in 0.1.2 [7].

**Modding.** The store data lists no mod support [1]. No official modding toolkit or plan was found in the official posts read.

**Client notes.** Windows only [1]; Linux unsupported [11]; Windows 11 update KB5124010 caused crash WD-L020, fixed 30 Sep 2026 [7].

text:
This document goes deeper than the parent foundation on WARDOGS aircraft (all helicopters in Early Access) and the systems that counter them. The Steam page lists helicopters in Early Access and fighter jets only for the full release [1]. Official Steam posts name only a few air facts: the Havoc, the Z20 Lakota, flare deployables, a vehicle fly-through reward cap, a Havoc cannon-damage bug fix, and a 2 Oct 2026 hotfix that disabled IR Rangefinders in the vendor and cut the time for the CIWS to destroy a Havoc from about 12 s to about 6 s [2][3][4].

The official 2 Oct balance post settles a press conflict: there were two separate hotfixes that day, a no-gameplay security and stability hotfix and, later, a balance hotfix [3][5]. The official post says "IR Rangefinders" (its title says "IR Goggles") [3].

The roster, prices and Pilot levels come only from player-reported guides, which conflict, so confidence is Medium. All values are a baseline before the Season 02 wipe due 15 Oct 2026 [6].

title: FOBs, Hammers & Base Building
topic: FOB deployment, supply types, hammer tiers, structures, pallet logistics, costs

text:
This document goes deeper than the parent foundation on forward operating bases (FOBs), the three hammer tiers, supply types, buildable structures and pallet logistics. It is a pre-Season-02 baseline: Season 02 is due 15 October 2026 and is expected to wipe progression, so every number is tabulated with its version and source class for mechanical diffing later.

The official Steam posts (saved locally and cited by Steam URL) settle the two conflicts the foundation left open. Large Hammer unlock moved from Support level 7 to level 8 in the Season 1 changelog, so level 8 is the current official value [1]. The Support-track Large Hammer unlock rose from $25,000 to $75,000 and the Medium Hammer unlock from $10,000 to $25,000 [1]. No source retrieved gives an $800 hammer price; see Open Questions. The FOB vendor price is $7,500 [1].

Confidence is Medium. Prices, levels and the 0.1.2 reward rules are official [1][2], but the build procedure, structure list, supply types and structure costs rest on player-reported guides [8][9][10], and no official text lists them.

text:
- Official, Season 1 (9 Sep 2026): FOB vendor price $2,500 to $7,500; Large Hammer vendor price $1,600 to $2,400 [1].
- Official, Season 1: Support-track unlocks are Medium Hammer $25,000 (was $10,000) and Large Hammer $75,000 (was $25,000), with Large Hammer level 7 to level 8 [1]. Level 8 is therefore the current value; level 7 is the pre-Season-1 value.
- Official, Update 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026): rewards for destroying buildables scale with build progress, so destroying a placed schematic no longer pays in full; pallets deposited into a FOB outside the zone award reduced rewards [2].
- Official, 0.1.2: buildable "crit spots" were reworked to favour a spot reachable from where the attacker stands [2].
- Player-reported: four supply types (Build, Ammo, Fuel, Mechanical); hammer tiers Small, Medium, Large; Build Supplies $10 each or $500 per 50 [8][9].
- Official design intent: building and destruction are core Early Access features, and a FOB fortifies a chokepoint [3][4].

text:
- **FOB**: player-deployed kit creating a build zone and supply storage; the official line is that players can build a forward operating base to fortify a chokepoint [4].
- **Hammer**: build tool in Small, Medium and Large tiers; the Support track sells the Medium and Large unlocks [1].
- **Pallet**: container used to deposit supplies into a FOB; 0.1.2 refers to depositing pallets into a FOB inside or outside the zone [2].
- **Schematic**: a placed, unbuilt structure; 0.1.2 refers to a "placed schematic" [2].
- **Build progress**: completion fraction of a buildable, which now scales destruction rewards [2].

As of Update 0.1.2 and the 2 Oct 2026 hotfixes (neither hotfix changed hammers, FOBs or pallets) [2][5][6].

- The FOB costs $7,500 at the vendor [1].
- The Large Hammer costs $2,400 at the vendor, and unlocks on the Support track at level 8 for $75,000; the Medium Hammer unlock is $25,000 [1].
- Destroying a buildable pays a reward scaled by its build progress [2].
- Depositing pallets into a FOB outside the zone pays a reduced reward [2].
- Buildable crit spots no longer reappear in the same place, get pushed into corners or jump to the far side of a structure [2].
- A crash involving buildables was fixed at Season 1 launch [1].
- The 2 Oct IR Goggles and CIWS hotfix made the CIWS destroy the Havoc in about 6 seconds instead of 12 [5]; guides list the CIWS as a Large-tier structure [8][10].

## Baseline values

Source class: Official = Steam announcement posts; Player = player-reported guide, not independently verified. "Season 1.0" is the 9 Sep 2026 changelog.

| Value | As-of version | Source |
|-------|---------------|--------|
| FOB vendor price $7,500 (was $2,500) | Season 1.0 | Official [1] |
| Large Hammer vendor price $2,400 (was $1,600) | Season 1.0 | Official [1] |
| Support: Medium Hammer unlock $25,000 (was $10,000) | Season 1.0 | Official [1] |
| Support: Large Hammer unlock $75,000 (was $25,000) | Season 1.0 | Official [1] |
| Support: Large Hammer unlock level 8 (was 7) | Season 1.0 | Official [1] |
| Medium Hammer unlock level 3 | Season 1 era | Player [8][9] |
| Small Hammer default, $100 | Season 1 era | Player [8][9] |
| Build Supplies $10 each, $500 per 50 | Season 1 era | Player [8] |
| Pilot: small armoured supply crate $10,000 (was $5,000) | Season 1.0 | Official [1] |
| Driver: Large Supply Crate unlock level 16 (was 20) | Season 1.0 | Official [1] |
| Driver: Kodiak Flatbed $35,000 (was $15,000), level 10 (was 2) | Season 1.0 | Official [1] |
| Supply crate purchase curve rescaled to 1-200 (was 25-250) | Season 1.0 | Official [1] |
| Supply crate item sold under $75: 1 XP (was 25 XP) | Season 1.0 | Official [1] |
| Buildable destruction reward scales with build progress (no figure published) | 0.1.2 | Official [2] |
| Pallet deposit outside FOB zone: reduced reward (no figure published) | 0.1.2 | Official [2] |
| Supply costs: Bunker 61, Mortar 91, Repair Station 121, Talon 601, CIWS 901, Drill Rig 1,351 | Season 1 era | Player [9] |
| CIWS kill time on Havoc about 6 seconds (was 12) | 2 Oct hotfix | Official [5] |

## FOB price and mechanics

The vendor price is the only officially published FOB number; the raise was made so the FOB and Large Hammer are "more of a choice" [1]. Official posts describe the FOB as a way to fortify a chokepoint and list building as an Early Access feature [3][4]. Player-reported procedure: deploy the kit on valid ground, not inside a building, a main base or another FOB's radius; deposit supplies into base storage through the FOB console; choose a structure from the build wheel; finish it with the hammer [8]. FOBs do not refill by themselves [9]. Enemies reaching the FOB console can reportedly hack the base, with a siren [8]. FOB count limits, radius and health are not published.

## The four supply types

All four are player-reported [8]; no official post names them.

| Supply type | Used by (player-reported) |
|-------------|--------------------------|
| Build | Structures; $10 each or $500 per 50 [8] |
| Ammo | Mortar, CIWS, SAM [8] |
| Fuel | Refuel Station, Drill Rig [8] |
| Mechanical | Repair Station [8] |

Official text confirms only supply crates as a purchasable item class (Pilot small armoured supply crate, Driver Large Supply Crate, Kodiak Flatbed) [1] and that helicopters can ferry supplies to teammates [4].

## Hammer tiers and unlocks

| Tier | Unlock | Structures needing the tier (player-reported) |
|------|--------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Small | Default; $100 (player-reported) [8][9] | Sandbags, barbed wire, hedgehogs, Recon Tent; no FOB needed [8] |
| Medium | Support track, $25,000 (official) [1]; level 3 (player-reported) [8][9] | HESCO, doors, gates [8] |
| Large | Support track, level 8, $75,000 (official) [1]; vendor $2,400 (official) [1] | Bunkers, Recon Towers, mortars, anti-air, Repair and Refuel Stations, Drill Rig [8] |

The required tier reportedly applies only to starting a blueprint; any hammer finishes it [8]. Hammers switch to Dismantle on finished objects and also repair [9].

Conflict resolution:

- **Level 7 versus 8.** The Season 1 changelog states "Large Hammer: level 7 to level 8" [1]. One guide still gave level 7 [9]; that is the pre-Season-1 value. Level 8 is the baseline.
- **$800 versus $25,000.** The official changelog gives $25,000 as the Medium Hammer Support unlock (previously $10,000) and as the former Large Hammer unlock, now $75,000 [1]. No retrieved official or press text gives an $800 hammer price. Any $800 figure is unsupported here; see Open Questions.
- **Vendor versus unlock.** The Support track gates the right to buy the hammer ($75,000, level 8), and the vendor charges $2,400 for a Large Hammer [1]. Whether the vendor price recurs per purchase is not stated.

## Buildable structures and costs

No official structure list or cost table exists in the posts retrieved. Player-reported supply costs [9]: Bunker 61, Mortar 91, Repair Station 121, Talon 601, CIWS 901, Drill Rig 1,351. Repair Stations repair and Refuel Stations refuel vehicles from stored supplies; the Drill Rig is reported to pull the Hot Zone toward a fuelled FOB [10]. Gates admit vehicles, doors are infantry-only, hedgehogs block vehicle routes [9]. Official: the CIWS was rebalanced on 2 Oct 2026 [5].

## Pallet delivery and the 0.1.2 reward reduction

Pallets are the logistics unit for moving supplies into a FOB; cargo vehicles carry small amounts and larger loads move on pallets (player-reported) [9]. Update 0.1.2 states: "Depositing pallets into a FOB outside the zone now awards reduced rewards" [2]. A press summary lists the same change among the cash and XP exploit fixes [7]. The size of the reduction and the zone boundary are not published. The post frames the change as anti-exploit and warns that players abusing repeatable exploits risk a permanent ban [2]. Supply crate sale XP was cut separately in Season 1 [1].

## Build-destroy interaction

Official: "Any rewards for destroying buildables now scale with their build progress - so destroying a placed schematic no longer gives a full reward" [2]. Rocket launchers can take down apartment blocks per the store page [4]. Player-reported: anything built can be destroyed, artillery can level fortifications from outside the zone, and unprotected pallets can be destroyed [8][9]. For diffing: reward scaling is by build progress, with no published curve.

text:
This is a pre-Season-02 baseline of every vehicle named in official WARDOGS text. The only official vehicle prices and unlock levels are in the Season 1 changelog posted on Steam on 9 Sep 2026 [1]. It names about a dozen vehicle entries and lists only the values it changed. It gives no complete roster, no crew sizes and no spawn prices. Everything else (spawn prices, the Gepard, the L2A6, the Havoc's price, the Lakota's level) is guide-only [5][6].

Where official text and the guides disagree, the official text wins and the conflict is recorded. The main findings: the guides' "Kodiak (pickup)" matches the official Kodiak Flatbed (Driver 10, $35,000 after the 10 Sep change) [1]. The official Lakota price is $35,000 but no official Lakota level exists, so the guides' Pilot 10 and Pilot 25 stay unresolved [1][5][6]. The Gepard and L2A6 do not appear in any official post retrieved.

Document confidence is Medium: the numbers that exist are official, but the roster is incomplete and the spawn-price column is player-reported only. Season 02 (due 15 Oct 2026) is expected to change these values.

text:
As of Update 0.1.2 plus the 2 Oct 2026 hotfixes:

- The changelog states "Artillery moved to Career level 90, and Heavy Tank moved to Driver level 35", and that Driver was "rejigged to give a satisfying escalation through attack vehicles" (9 Sep 2026) [1].
- Official ground unlock levels: URAL 3, Kodiak Assault 6, Dune Buggy 8, Kodiak Flatbed 10, URAL Covered 18, URAL Attack 25, Humvee with minigun 30, Heavy Tank 35 [1].
- Official unlock prices: Dune Buggy $25,000, URAL $35,000, Kodiak Flatbed $35,000, Artillery Tank $500,000, Little Bird with miniguns $50,000, Z20 Lakota $35,000 [1].
- Update 0.1.2 (30 Sep 2026) capped rewards from the vehicle fly-through exploit, fixed a Havoc taking too much damage from 20mm and 30mm cannon fire, and blocked throwables from enclosed vehicle seats [2].
- The 2 Oct 2026 hotfix made the CIWS destroy the Havoc in about 6 seconds instead of 12, with no downtime or client download [3].
- Each player starts their journey with $10,000 and buys a loadout per life from weapons, gear, utility and vehicles [4].

## Reconciliation of the foundation's conflicts

| Vehicle | Foundation guide values | Official text | Resolution |
|---------|-------------------------|---------------|------------|
| Kodiak (pickup) | Driver 10, $35,000 [6]; $3,000 or $2,500 spawn | "Kodiak Flatbed: level 2 to level 10", "$15,000 to $35,000" [1] | The guide's "pickup" equals the Flatbed (Inferred by matching level and price). Unlock figures confirmed; spawn price still guide-only. |
| Kodiak M249 / Assault | Driver 6, $50,000 [6] | "Kodiak Assault: level 8 to level 6" [1] | Level confirmed. The $50,000 is not in the changelog, so it stays guide-only. |
| Z20 Lakota | Pilot 10 [5]; Pilot 25 [6]; $35,000 | Pilot track, "$50,000 to $35,000"; no level [1] | Price confirmed. Level is unresolved because the official text gives none and the guides disagree. |
| Flakpanzer Gepard | $10,000 or about $8,000; "Wardog track" | Not mentioned | Guide-only. Official track names are Driver, Pilot, Career, Support, Recon and Medic [1]; "Wardog" is not one of them, which suggests the guide means Career (Inferred). |
| L2A6 | about $14,000 as the heavy tank | Only "Heavy Tank", Driver 35 [1] | Whether the Heavy Tank is the L2A6 is Inferred only; no official post uses the name. |
| URAL Defender and M249 | Driver 18 and 25 [6] | "URAL Covered" level 18, "URAL Attack" level 25 [1] | Levels match, names differ; the guide names are likely the same variants (Inferred). |
| Humvee minigun | Driver 30 [6] | Driver 30 [1] | Agrees. |
| Artillery | $500,000, Career 90 | $500,000, Career 90 [1] | Agrees. |

## Role notes (official)

Vehicle turrets now have a maximum operator rotation speed, helicopter input damping applies to every input device, the Lakota had a balance pass, a pitch fix and a 6 dB chase camera rattle reduction, and a DPI issue affecting tank aiming was fixed (10 Sep 2026) [1]. The Steam page promotes tanks, an artillery tank and helicopters that ferry supplies to teammates [4]. Vehicle roles beyond these are Inferred from names.

text:
WARDOGS pairs a combined-arms vehicle set (tanks, an artillery tank, helicopters, light ground vehicles) with player-built Forward Operating Bases (FOBs) and a destructible battlefield. Bulkhead's own posts confirm that Early Access includes "Grounded Gunplay & Vehicles" and "Destruction & Build Mechanics" [5], and the Steam page promotes tanks, an artillery tank, helicopters that ferry supplies, a buildable forward operating base and apartment blocks that rocket launchers can destroy [6].

This revision replaces the v1.0.0 reliance on press summaries with the full official Steam text. The Season 1 changelog (9 Sep 2026) is the only official source for vehicle and hammer prices and unlock levels, and it lists changes only, not a full table [1]. Official values now confirmed: FOB vendor $7,500, Large Hammer vendor $2,400, Medium Hammer unlock $25,000, Large Hammer unlock $75,000 at Support level 8, Kodiak Flatbed Driver 10 for $35,000, Heavy Tank Driver 35, Artillery Tank Career 90 for $500,000 [1]. Update 0.1.2 fixed the vehicle fly-through exploit, reduced pallet rewards outside the FOB zone and scaled buildable-destruction rewards by build progress [2]. The 2 Oct balance hotfix made the CIWS destroy a Havoc in about 6 seconds instead of 12 [3].

Still player-reported only: per-spawn vehicle prices, the build procedure, supply types, structure costs and which hammer tier builds what [7][8][9][10][11]. Document confidence is Medium: prices, levels and patch changes are official, but the roster is incomplete and the mechanics layer is guide-sourced. For depth see vehicle-roster-and-prices, fob-and-base-building and air-and-counter-air.

All facts as of 2026-10-08, Update 0.1.2 plus the 2 Oct hotfixes.

- Early Access includes "Grounded Gunplay & Vehicles" and "Destruction & Build Mechanics" [5]. Squads provide "vehicle locking" [5].

It also fixed a Havoc bug that raised damage taken from 20mm and 30mm cannon fire and blocked throwables from enclosed vehicle seats [2].
- The 2 Oct 2026 security and stability hotfix announcement says a hotfix is planned for 08:00 UTC with about one hour of downtime; it lists no gameplay changes [4]. A separate 2 Oct balance hotfix disabled IR Rangefinders in the vendor until Season 02 and cut the CIWS time to destroy a Havoc from about 12 s to about 6 s [3].

text:
## Vehicle roster

Only the Season 1 changelog gives official vehicle values, and only for what it changed [1]. Full tables, conflicts and labels are in vehicle-roster-and-prices. Spawn prices are the per-purchase cost and are player-reported only [7][10]; "unlock" is the one-time track price, a reading Inferred from the changelog's track headings [1].

| Class | Vehicle | Official track, level and unlock | Spawn price (player-reported) |
|-------|---------|----------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Ground | Dune Buggy | Driver 8, $25,000 [1] | not published |
| Ground | URAL | Driver 3, $35,000 [1] | $6,000 [10] |
| Ground | URAL Covered / URAL Attack | Driver 18 / Driver 25 [1] | not published |
| Ground | Kodiak Assault | Driver 6 [1] | $3,750 [7][10] |
| Ground | Kodiak Flatbed | Driver 10, $35,000 (was level 2, $15,000) [1] | $2,500 [7]; $3,000 [10] |
| Ground | Humvee with minigun | Driver 30 [1] | $4,500 [7] |
| Ground | Heavy Tank | Driver 35 (was Career 35) [1] | about $14,000, "L2A6" unconfirmed [7] |
| Ground | Artillery Tank | Career 90, $500,000 (was Career 55, $400,000) [1] | about $8,000 [7] |
| Air | Little Bird with miniguns | Pilot, $50,000 (was $25,000); level not stated [1] | $7,000 [10] |
| Air | Z20 Lakota | Pilot, $35,000 (was $50,000); level not stated [1] | $7,400 [7]; $8,000 [10] |
| Air | Havoc | named in 0.1.2 and the CIWS hotfix; track, level and price not stated [2][3] | about $18,000, Pilot 35 [7] |

Guide-only rows with no official counterpart: Bobcat quad, base and M249 Humvee, Flakpanzer Gepard (a guide's "Wardog track" has no official counterpart; the six official tracks are listed under Definitions), AH-6M/AH-6R and the team armoured spawn vehicle [7][10]. Guide names such as "Kodiak (pickup)" match the official Kodiak Flatbed by level and price (Inferred). Season 1 also gave the Z20 Lakota a balance pass and pitch fix, capped vehicle turret operator rotation speed, applied helicopter input damping to every input device, fixed a DPI issue affecting tank aiming and reduced Lakota chase-camera rattle by 6 dB [1]. No naval vehicles appear in any source retrieved.

## Purchasing and delivery

Official: vehicles are bought with cash as part of the per-life loadout [5][6]. Player-reported flow [7][10]:

1. Stand at the Vehicle Vendor stall in the safe zone and choose a vehicle in the LAND or AIR tab.
2. Pay the one-time unlock if the vehicle is gated, then the spawn price on each purchase, with no confirmation prompt [10].
3. The vehicle appears for the buyer; armed variants cost more and die to the same anti-vehicle weapons [7].

Free options reported by one guide only: a team armoured spawn vehicle unlocked at 20 team points with a satellite dish that disables it if destroyed, plus free transport helicopters and SUVs a few minutes into a match [10]. Cargo vehicles carry small supply amounts and larger loads move on pallets (player-reported) [9]. The store page says helicopters can ferry supplies to teammates [6]. External sling-loading is unconfirmed in every source read; see air-and-counter-air.

## FOB construction

Official prices and levels [1], player-reported mechanics [8][9]. Full detail is in fob-and-base-building.

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| FOB kit | $7,500 vendor price as of Season 1 (was $2,500) [1] |
| Small Hammer | default, $100 (player-reported) [8][9] |
| Medium Hammer | Support track, unlock $25,000 (was $10,000) [1]; level 3 is player-reported [8][9] |
| Large Hammer | Support level 8 (was 7), unlock $75,000 (was $25,000) [1]; vendor price $2,400 (was $1,600) [1] |
| Build Supplies | $10 each or $500 for a 50 stack (player-reported) [8] |

The "$800" hammer figure and the Large Hammer level 7 in earlier drafts are superseded or unsourced: level 7 was the pre-Season-1 value [1], and no official or press text gives $800. Procedure (player-reported): deploy the kit on valid ground (not inside a building, a main base or another FOB's radius), deposit supplies via the FOB console, pick a structure from the build wheel and hit the yellow X markers [8]. Small Hammer structures (sandbags, barbed wire, hedgehogs, Recon Tent) need no FOB; HESCO, doors and gates need Medium; bunkers, Recon Towers, mortars, anti-air, Repair and Refuel Stations and the Drill Rig need Large; the tier applies only to starting a blueprint [8]. Reported build costs include Bunker 61, Mortar 91, Repair Station 121, Talon 601, CIWS 901 and Drill Rig 1,351 supplies [9]. Supply types reported: Build, Ammo, Fuel and Mechanical [8]. The Drill Rig is reported to pull the Hot Zone toward a fuelled FOB [11]. No official post lists structures or supply costs.

## Destruction

Official: the store page says players can "Destroy apartment blocks with rocket launchers or tear your way through towns in heavily armoured tanks" [6], and the FAQ calls the battlefield "large-scale" and destructible [5]. Update 0.1.2 scales buildable-destruction rewards by build progress and reworked buildable crit spots so they favour a spot reachable from where the attacker stands [2]; a buildables crash was fixed at Season 1 [1]. Player-reported: anything built can be destroyed, artillery can level fortifications from outside the zone, hammers switch to Dismantle on finished objects and also repair, unprotected pallets can be destroyed, and enemies at the FOB console can hack the base with a siren [8][9]. Vehicles: a destroyed vehicle must be re-bought, and a damaged one can be repaired at a Repair Station using Mechanical Supplies (player-reported) [7][10]. No source gives structure health values. See destructibility-and-level-design for terrain and building destruction.
